title: Weekly Review of the Slovene Economy from 16 to 22 September.
text:
Ljubljana, 24 September (STA) - At Thursday's session the government conceded to the demands of Slovene transport workers and reduced the petrol tax on diesel oil by 11.3 percent, thus preventing protests around the country. At its session the government also decided to dismiss the Acting General Manager of Slovenia's electricity supplier (ELES) Vekoslav Korosec and replaced him with Vitoslav Turk, the head of the trade department in ELES. According to the electricity supplier, the decision to dismiss Korosec is based on changes to the act on the government and to the ELES statute, while Korosec believes that the move is purely of a political nature. 

 CHRONOLOGY: SATURDAY, 16 September LJUBLJANA - The average selling price of natural gas from the underground network increased by seven percent to stand at SIT 36.22 per litre. 

 MONDAY, 18 September LJUBLJANA - Robert S. Kaplan, the world's leading management authority was on visit to Slovenia upon the invitation of Gospodarski vestnik publishing house and company Aktiva Group. The method of measuring business excellence called the Balanced Scorecard (BSC), Kaplan's brainchild, was presented to over 300 Slovene economists and businessmen. The BSC has been one of the most influential business ideas for the past 75 years. LJUBLJANA - The Slovene Development Corporation (SRD) finished its marathon session at which the annual report for 1999 and operation in the first five months of 2000 was discussed. At the session the conditions in certain Slovene companies currently under SRD control was also discussed. 

 TUESDAY, 19 September LJUBLJANA - Prices of petrol increased around the whole country. The price of the most widely used 95-Octane Eurosuper increased by SIT 4.3 to SIT 153.8. LJUBLJANA - The 11th Furniture Fair in Ljubljana opened its doors. The guest speaker, Minister for Economic Affairs Joze Zagozen, stressed that the Slovene wood industry needs to create export-orientated products, which will assist to increase competitiveness and the level of value added on foreign markets. LJUBLJANA - The Bank of Slovenia completed its two-month intervention in the foreign exchange market during which it set a base exchange rate and a maximum ratio between the purchase and the selling rates. The 21 banks which signed a co-operation contract with the central bank in March will therefore be able to set their purchase and selling exchange rates independently. The aim of such an intervention by the central bank was to curtail rapid increases of foreign currencies as the growth of exchange rates was estimated to be too fast at the time of the intervention. 

 WEDNESDAY, 22 September MARIBOR - The management of the Maribor-based bank Nova KBM signed a borrowing contract to the value of 5 million euros with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). 

 THURSDAY, 21 September LJUBLJANA - At its weekly session the government decided to reduce excise duties on diesel oil by 11.3 percent and thus kept the promise given by the government negotiating team to the Union of Slovene Transporters (SAS) earlier this week. Other demands of the bus and lorry drivers were also met, so the SAS ceased all their activities regarding public protests and road blockages. LJUBLJANA - At its weekly session the government decided to dismiss acting General Manager of Slovenia's electricity supplier (ELES) Vekoslav Korosec. In turn the Ministry of Economic Affairs proposed that Vitoslav Turk, the head of the trade department in ELES, should replace Korosec 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Slovenia's Central Bank Ceases Intervention in Foreign Exchange Market The Bank of Slovenia on Tuesday completed a two-month period of intervening in the foreign exchange market by setting a base exchange rate and a maximum ratio between the purchase and the selling rates. The 21 banks which signed a co-operation contract with the central bank in March will therefore be able to set their purchase and selling exchange rates independently. The aim of such an intervention by the central bank was to curtail rapid increases of foreign currencies as the growth of exchange rates was estimated to be too fast at the time of the intervention. 

 BANKS NKBM Signs a Borrowing Contract with EBRD The management of the Maribor-based bank Nova KBM on Wednesday signed a borrowing contract to the value of 5 million euros with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). The NKBM will grant favourable investment loans to entrepreneurs and companies with up to one hundred employees for the financing of new business projects. The interest rates for the loans with the redemption period of up to five years will be EURO LIBOR + 2.5 percent. Clients can get a loan to the value of up to 125,000 euros. 

 COMPANIES Tyre Producer Issues Bid to Take Over Chemical Company Sava, a Slovene tyre producer, on Friday issued a bid to purchase shares of the chemical company Color Medvode. The takeover bid follows Sava's new strategy to launch a new line of activities in the company focusing on the rubber industry, chemistry, trade and tourism. The bid refers to 845,832 ordinary registered shares, 104,559 of which are already owned by Sava. The share's nominal value is SIT 2,000 (9.6 euros). Sava has offered five of its ordinary registered shared for 19 Color shares, or SIT 4,000 for one Color share. The offer closes on 20 October. 

 Telekom Shareholders to Receive Dividends of 1.5 Euro per Share Shareholders of Telekom, Slovenia's telephone services provider, adopted a decision at a general meeting on Thursday, to pay out dividends for 1999 in the amount of SIT 2.026 billion (9.7 million euro) or SIT 310 (1.5 euro) per share. Gross profits from 1995 with a revalued adjustment in the amount of SIT 76.2 million, gross profits from 1996 in the amount of SIT 612.4 million, and SIT 1.337 billion gross profits in 1997 will be used for dividends. Half of gross profits from 1999 in the amount of SIT 3.949 billion will remain undistributed, while the other half has already been placed in company reserves. 

 Emo Receives ISO 14001 Ecology Standard Certificate Celje-based (76km east of Ljubljana) tools' manufacturer Emo Tools received the ISO 14001 ecology standard certificate. DM 350,000 have been spent in an effort to acquire the "green standard" certificate, which was launched back in 1998, said Renato Fijavz, in charge of the office for quality at Emo Tools, and added that the main reason behind this undertaking was to raise ecological awareness of the employees. 

 Brest Furniture Company Receives ISO 14001 Ecology Green Standard Certificate The furniture producer Brest presented the first electronic shop in Slovenia's furniture industry and four new furniture lines and thus presented itself at the 11th Furniture Fair in Ljubljana, which opened its doors on Tuesday. The Cerknica-based (some 40 km south of Ljubljana) furniture company, employing around 400 workers, also received the ISO 14001 green standard certificate. It is one of the first Slovene companies to receive such quality certificate for improving ecological conditions. 

 INDUSTRY Government Adopts Programme for Privatisation of Steel Industry At its session on Thursday the government adopted a programme for the privatisation of the Slovene steel industry. The programme envisages state assistance until 2003 to the amount of 210 million euros. The programme foresees the privatisation of core companies in the steel industry by 2002, while non-core companies would be privatised by the end of the year. The number of employees in the core companies of the Slovene steel industry is set to fall from 3000 to 2500. 

 STATISTICS 11.9-Percent Unemployment Rate in July The national statistics office recorded a labour force of 874,554 people in July, 770,167 of whom were persons in employment, a drop of 0.3 percent from June, but a 0.9 percent increase on a year-to-year comparison. According to the statistics office, the level of registered unemployment stood at 11.9 percent in July, a rise of 0.1 percentage point over June. 

 STOCK MARKET As many as 6,654 deals were closed last week on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange. The overall turnover totaled SIT 2.76 billion (13 million euros), one billion of which accounted for lot deals. Most share indices were down last week, as the SBI share index lost 0.77 percent to stand at 1666.62 points at Friday's close. The free market index IPT was up 1.05 percent to 981.06 points, while the authorised investment companies' index PIX decreased by 0.35 percent to finish at 1273.11 points on Friday. 

FOREIGN EXCHANGE The Slovene tolar strengthened against the U.S. dollar during the week; the dollar stood at SIT 239.61, down SIT 1.63, on Friday. However, the tolar weakened against the major European currencies: it was down SIT 0.54 at SIT 136.88 against the Swiss franc and down SIT 0.18 at SIT 208.44 against the euro. One Deutsche mark stood at SIT 106.57 up SIT 0.09, while the Austrian schilling strengthened by SIT 0.02 to be worth SIT 15.15. 100 Italian lira remained level against the tolar at SIT 10.76. title: Bank of  Slovenia  ends  forex intervention .
text:
LJUBLJANA, Sept 18 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Monday it was ending its two-month intervention on the foreign exchange market that was designed to slow down the tolar's depreciation. 

 The intervention started on July 18 when the central bank told commercial banks to buy euros at a minimum rate of 207.12 tolars and to sell at a maximum of 207.96 tolars.

title: Slovenia 's  Central Bank  to Cease  Intervention  in  Foreign Exchange  Market.
text:
Ljubljana, 18 September (STA) - The Bank of Slovenia will soon complete a two-month period of intervening in the foreign exchange market by setting a base exchange rate and a maximum ratio between the purchase and the selling rates. 21 banks which signed a co-operation contract with the central bank in March will therefore be able to set their purchase and selling exchange rates independently as of 19 September, the Bank of Slovenia reported on Monday. 

 The aim of such an intervention by the central bank was to curtail rapid increases of foreign currencies as the growth of exchange rates was estimated to be too fast at the time of the intervention. 

 As of 18 July, the 21 contracting banks were obliged to buy foreign currencies in the corporate sector for a minimum of SIT 207.1249 per euro and sell currencies for a maximum of SIT 207.9551 per euro. The highest ratio between the purchase and the selling rates was set at 0.2 percent. (konec)ar/eho STA023 2000-09-18/16:13.

title: Central Bank  Will  Intervene  on the  Foreign Exchange  Market.
text:
Ljubljana, 17 July (STA) - The Bank of Slovenia will intervene on the foreign exchange market on Tuesday because it believes that the current growth in exchange rates is too high. According to a press release published on Monday, the central bank fixed the base exchange rate at SIT 207.54 for one euro with a difference of up to 0.2 percent. 

 The intervention is possible under a special contract signed between the Bank of Slovenia and 21 Slovene banks last March. 

 On the basis of the base exchange rate and the difference the lowest buying rate and the highest selling rate are calculated. The banks that signed the contract with the central bank are obliged to buy and sell at the agreed price. On the market serving companies foreign exchange will be purchased at no less than SIT 207,1249 a euro and sold at up to SIT 207.9551 a euro as of 18 July. In exchange offices rates calculated in euro may differ up to 0.2 percent up from the highest selling rate and down from the lowest buying rate for the German mark and up to 0.4 percent for other currencies of the EMU members, Switzerland, Great Britain and the U.S. 

 The Bank of Slovenia will change the base exchange rate in line with trends on the foreign exchange market and domestic money market and in accordance to the goals of its monetary policy. (konec)ep STA013 2000-07-17/15:52.

title: Bank of  Slovenia  to end tolar rate  intervention .
text:
LJUBLJANA, Aug 25 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Wednesday it would discontinue imposing an intervention selling rate for euros and German marks implemented on July 19. 

 "From August 26, the chosen banks are no longer obliged to maintain the intervention selling rate," the central bank said in a statement. 

 From July 19, banks included in the intervention were selling foreign currency to companies at a maximum of 197.37 tolars to the euro and at 100.91 tolars to the mark. 

 Analysts said the intervention was ended because commercial banks' rates had already started falling. 

 This week banks sold euros to companies at an average of 197.16 tolars and around 100.80 tolars per mark. 

 "The intervention had no sense any longer, the central bank was still limiting growth of rates which were already falling," said Dusan Kosanovic, head of treasury at Societe Generale. 

 He said the rates were likely to continue falling over the short-term but would become more volatile in September when corporate demand for foreign exchange is expected to increase. ((Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-546, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from 17 through 23 July.
text:
Ljubljana, 25 July (STA) - The government endorsed an increase in the prices of oil derivatives and liquidised natural gas at a session on Thursday. The price of petrol increased by 9.9 percent, the VAT excluded, while the retail price including the VAT rose by 3.4 percent to SIT 123.9 (DM 1.2). 

 As of 24 July a litre of 91-octane unleaded petrol costs SIT 110, a litre of 95-octane SIT 110.6 and a litre of 98-octane unleaded petrol SIT 115.80. The price of liquidised gas in bottles was raised by 8.9 percent from SIT 127.89 to SIT 139.27 per one kilogram. The estimated impact on the consumer prices index is 0.15 percent in case of petrol and 0.003 percent in case of liquidised gas. Major reasons for the price raises are an increase in the exchange rate of the U.S. dollar and in a surge of crude oil prices on the world market. 

 INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION SID Signed an Agreement with Macedonian Development Bank 

 Slovene Export Corporation (SID) and Macedonian Development Bank signed a bilateral cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening bilateral economic relations. According to SID chairman Marjan Kramar, the agreement represents a basis for further cooperation between the two countries that share the same goal - economic development. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Bank of Slovenia Intervenes in the Foreign Exchange Market 

 The Bank of Slovenia (BS) introduced on 19 July an intervention sales rate in the foreign exchange market. Six banks - Abanka, SKB banka, LB Banka Zasavje, Banka Velenje, Banka Koper and Nova Ljubljanska banka - can sell foreign exchange at SIT 197.37 to the euro and SIT 100.91 to the German mark at maximum. The exchange rate in exchange offices can be 0.2 percent out at the most for the German mark and 0.4 percent for other EMU countries, Switzerland, Great Britain and the U.S. 

Foreign Exchange Reserves at 4.5 Billion in End-May 

 Slovenia had US$ 4.458 billion of foreign currency reserves at the end of May. The reserves decreased by US$ 151.3 million m/m, coming short of the nation's total external debt of US$ 5.224 billion by US$ 786 million, the Bank of Slovenia reported in the June issue of its Bulletin. Reserves of the central bank made up US$ 3.438 billion and those of other banks US$ 1020 million. 

 Exchange Offices Turn Over DM 735 Million in a Month 

 Exchange offices in Slovenia turned over almost 735 million German marks last June. The foreign currency purchased amounted to DM 369 million and exceeded the amount of the foreign currency sold by DM 3 million. June's turnover marked a rise of 4.7 percent (DM 33.3 million) in a year-on-year comparison. Bureaux de change turned over DM 3.706 billion in the first half of this year, the purchase totalling DM 30 million and surmounting the sale by 1.6 percent. The turnover was down by DM 402 million over the same period last year. The mean exchange rate for the German mark averaged SIT 99.81 last June. Last year about 330 exchange points across the country turned over almost DM 8.2 billion. 

 BANKS Dolenjska Banka Successful in the First Half of 1999 

 The Dolenjska banka bank made a profit in the value of SIT 330 million in the first six 1999 months, which is slightly more than a half of the 1998 profit. The total assets grew up by 2.7 percent to SIT 79.5 billion in the same period. With an approximately three-percent market share, the bank is placed ninth among Slovene commercial banks. 

 COMPANIES Talks on N-Plant Carried On Despite HEP's Statement 

 Talks between Slovenia and Croatia on a settlement of outstanding issues related to the jointly owned Krsko N-plant are under way at full speed at all levels despite a statement by a senior manager of the Croatian electricity supplier (HEP) that HEP would like to sell its share in the plant, the Slovene Economics Ministry told STA. The ministry explained it had not received from HEP any official information about the sell of its share in the Krsko plant. According to the ministry, both Slovenia and Croatia would like to sign the agreement on the plant which would define the status and ownership of the plant as soon as possible. The ministry added that the Croatian partner in negotiations is not HEP, but the government. President of HEP Board Damir Begovic informed the public about his company's intention to sell its share in the plant at a press conference in Zagreb. He said the opening price would be around one billion German marks. 

 WAGES Minimum Salary Rises by 6.3 Percent 

 The Economic and Social Council raised the minimum salary by 6.3 percent to SIT 72,521 (DM 725). The increase takes effect from 1 August. Trade union representatives stressed the importance of establishing adequate salaries ratio between manufacturing and non-manufacturing sectors. The Economic and Social Council decided to launch discussion and analysis of the ratios this autumn in order to eliminate any discord with the agreement on salaries policy. 

 Telekom Received the SAP CCC Certificate 

 The Slovene telecommunications company Telekom was the first company in Slovenia to receive the SAP CCC (Customer Competence Center) Certificate. SAP is an integrated information system backing information support in companies, used by more than 200 companies of the kind worldwide. The SAP system is used in approximately 20 Slovene companies. 

 PRIVATISATION SIT 101 Billion Available for Privatisation Gap 

 The total value of property available to fill the privatisation gap amounts to SIT 101.1 billion (DM 1 billion). As the overall privatisation deficit amounts to SIT 179.7 billion according to the latest government estimates the difference will be covered by financial assets of the state, completion of the decree on securing state property and by increasing the share of investments of the Slovene Development Corporation (SRD). Government committees have already discussed a bill on state property privatisation, which is expected to be submitted to the parliament soon. 

 TOURISM Slovene Tourist Board Opens Information Office in Zagreb 

 The Slovene Tourist Board has recently opened its information office in the Croatian capital, Zagreb, to enhance its promotional activity in Croatia, a country from which a lot of foreign tourists spend their holidays in Slovenia. As to tourist nights spent in Slovenia, Croatia places fourth (211,863 in 1998) after Germany, Italy and Austria. To reduce the cost of promotion, the board has opened the office in Zagreb in collaboration with the Zagreb branch office of Slovenia's tour organiser Kompas Turizem. To attract foreign tourists in the 1999/2000 season, the board has already decided on three major promotions (in Vienna, Munich and Milan). Moreover, it will use six information offices (London, Zurich, New York, Rotterdam, Budapest and Zagreb) for additional campaigns and the provision of information about Slovenia. 

 Nearly 10-Percent Drop in Tourist Income in January-to-May Period 

 The influx of foreign currency from tourism fell 9.9 percent in the first five months of 1999 from the same period last year, the latest data from the Tourist and Restaurant Business Association at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GZS) show. All five months saw a drop in foreign currency, but a 3-percent rise in foreign tourist nights was recorded in the period before the war broke out in Yugoslavia. In March, the gambling industry recorded the sharpest decline of over 25 percent from a year earlier. Interestingly, the influx of foreign currency from foreign tourists into Slovene tourist companies was above last year's figures. Tourist companies' revenues make up 17.8 percent of the entire inflow of foreign currency from tourism into the country (14.9 percent in 1998). Foreigners continue to buy less in Slovene duty-free shops; a drop of 7.8 percent was recorded in the first five months from the same period a year earlier. With the number of Slovene tourists up 9 percent in the first five months, th total number of tourists only fell by 2 percent. 

 Tourist Industry Figures Turn Downwards at Bled 

 Hotels and camps in the Alpine resort of Bled (northwest) recorded a 16-percent decrease in bookings in the first half of July over the same period last year, the local tourist association reported. From 1 to 18 July tourist facilities in Bled accommodated 24,723 persons, among which 22,099 were foreigners and 2,624 Slovenes. The number of tourist nights by foreign subjects decreased by 19 percent in a year-on-year comparison, while the number of those by domestic tourists increased by 41 percent. 

 SHOPS The Sales Begin 

 The majority of Slovene clothing and shoe shops and department stores started the sales on 20 July. The sale prices are 20 to 40 percent of the normal price on average. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE LSE Supervisory Board Meets 

 The Supervisory Board of the Ljubljana Stock Exchange (LSE) discussed and adopted a report on the LSE operations, on the half-year LSE performance and on the project of a new stock exchange information system (BIS). 

 Dullness on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange 

 Trading on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange was calm last week. The SBI share index closed the week at 1770.66 points, up 0.81 points compared to last Friday; the BIO bond index lost 0.09 points to close the week at 106.76. From Monday to Wednesday, only SIT 160 million were turned over, while on Thursday the trade amounted to SIT 100 million due to two package deals (SIT 71 million with the Hoteli Bernardin bonds and SIT 31 million with the third issue SKB bonds). On Friday, the trade totalled SIT 1.223 billion due to package deals with the tenth issue treasury bonds in the value of SIT 707 million and with the Dolenjska banka shares in the value of SIT 356 million. 

 EXCHANGE RATES Higher Exchange Rates of Foreign Currencies

 All major foreign currencies saw their exchange rates rise according to the Bank of Slovenia mean exchange rate over the past week. The Euro rose by SIT 0.3 to SIT 195.7, German mark added SIT 0.2 to SIT 100.1, and Swiss franc edged up by SIT 0.2 to SIT 121.9. Austrian schilling and Italian lira remained flat at SIT 14.2 and SIT 10.1 respectively. The U.S. dollar dropped by SIT 5.4 to SIT 186.3.

title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from 10 through 16 July.
text:
Ljubljana, 18 July (STA) - The absence of a negotiated agreement on the Krsko Nuclear Power Plant (NEK) was claimed by official sources to be the main reason for postponing the meeting of Slovene and Croatian government delegations this week, at which the countries were to sign the NEK agreement and the bilateral property agreement. Following their meeting on Friday, Economics Ministers of Slovenia and Croatia, Tea Petrin and Nenad Porges, were positive about the progress made by negotiating teams, announcing the tams would settle the remaining problems over the next days. 

 First steps were also taken this week to close the notorious privatisation gap, the difference between the value of privatisation vouchers issued to population and that of the property to be privatised. The First Pension Fund Act took effect offering Privatisation Investment Fund (PIF) shareholders the option to exchange their shares for pension vouchers; the latter may be sold later on or invested to the First Pension Fund. According to the Association of Management Companies, which presented its view on the act on 12 July, the monthly rate is more favourable for older persons. The entry into force of the First Pension Act at the same started the three year period during which PIFs must transform to ordinary investment or joint stock companies. 

 Two weeks after the value added tax was introduced, the Finance Ministry estimated VAT's effects were as expected. Prices of food and non-alcoholic beverages rose by 2.63 percent and prices of restaurant services by 2.34 percent according to preliminary estimates, while the prices of those goods that should be cheaper because of lower tax rates in most cases did not change. Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur announced that government-controlled prices would be gradually adjusted by September. 

 Chronology: Tuesday/13 July - Ljubljana: First Pension Fund Bill takes effect. Wednesday/14 July - Ljubljana: Meeting of Transport Ministers of Slovenia and Croatia, Anton Bergauer and Zeljko Luzavac. Wednesday/14 July - Zagreb: Export Corporation of Slovenia and the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development sign cooperation agreement. Friday/16 July - Strmol: Working meeting of Economics Ministers of Slovenia and Croatia, Tea Petrin and Nenad Porges, and of negotiation groups for the Krsko Nuclear Power Plant (NEK). Friday/16 July: National Assembly passes Regional Development Promotion Act and the 1999 Government Intervention in Agriculture Act. 

 INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION 

 Slovene-Ukrainian Commission on Economic Co-Operation Sign Protocol 

 The Slovene and Ukrainian delegations signed, on 16 July, a protocol of the first meeting of the Slovene-Ukrainian commission on co-operation in economy and trade. Co-operation between the two countries is relatively low, with the full volume of trade amounting to only US$ 58 million. This year's data regarding the growth in the past years even indicate a fall of the volume of trade which decreased almost by one half this year over the past year. However, the commission agreed there are still huge potentials to increase trade between the two countries, with medicines and pharmaceutical products being the area with the most possibilities for the co-operation of companies. 

 Slovene Export Corporation Signs Agreement on Co-Operation with a Croatian Bank 

 The Slovene Export Corporation (SID) and the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) signed an agreement on co-operation in Zagreb on 14 July. The aim of the agreement is to provide support to export activities of the Slovene and Croatian companies on local markets as well as the markets in third countries. To date SID has mainly co-operated with HBOR in information exchange. 

 Slovene Food Companies in the U.S. 

 A Slovene business delegation led by the chairman of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia, Mr. Cveto Stantic, started a seven-day visit to the United States on 12 July to attend the Fancy Food trade show in New York, business conferences in New York and Cleveland, and meet representatives U.S. food companies. The delegation also attended a seminar on export potentials of Slovene companies in the U.S. 

 PRICES Government-Controlled Prices to be Adjusted by September 

 Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur announced on 12 July that government-controlled prices for all groups of products would be adjusted on a gradual basis until September after they had been frozen temporarily because of the introduction of VAT. Among the first steps according to Senjur will be to raise gasoline and electricity prices, although this will not be due to VAT but to higher crude oil prices and a stronger dollar. In turn, electricity prices will only change after the base prices without VAT influences is calculated. By the end of September other controlled prices will be adjusted as well, including the prices of public transportation, gas and public hygiene. Prices of obligatory school books, telecom services and post services will not change according to Senjur. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Central Bank Chooses Six Banks for Intervention Exchange Rate 

 The Bank of Slovenia chose six banks which will be obliged to sell foreign currencies at an intervention selling rate in case the central bank decides to introduce an intervention period. These banks inlcude: Abanka, SKB, LB Banka Zasavje, Banka Velenje, Banka Koper and NLB (Nova Ljubljanska banka). From 19 July on, the banks will be allowed to sell Euro at a maximum of SIT 197.37, and Deutsche mark at no more than SIT 100.91. Exchange offices and the selected banks are also allowed to sell foreign cash at rates that exceed the set central bank rate by a maximum of 0.2 percent (DM) and by a maximum of 0.4 percent for currencies of the EMU member states, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States. 

 BANKS Higher Interest Rates on Deposits in August 

 As recommended by the Association of Slovene Banks, higher interest rates on deposits will take effect on 1 August after 19 out of 25 banks have backed the recommendation. Interest rates on over three-month deposits will thus be higher by 0.25 to 0.50 percentage point. The 19 banks that went along with the measure account for 91 percent of the Slovene banking system's total assets. 

 COMPANIES Petrol, Ina Sign Precontract to Establish Joint Venture 

 Petrol CEO Janez Lotric and Director General of Croatia's INA, Davor Stern, signed a precontract to sell the stock of the Interina corporation which is owned by Ina Zagreb. The contract was a precondition for the two oil companies to sign a contract establishing a Slovenia-based joint venture to market liquified oil gas. 

 Lower Sales and Profits for Color this Year 

 The chemicals manufacturer Color made SIT 3.18 billion of sales this year, down by 4.2 percent y/y. Profits in the period dropped by 12 percent to SIT 185.2 million. 

 Autocommerce Buys Perftech 

 Ljubljana-based Autocommerce trade company bought late last week the controlling share of the Bled-based Perftech internet provider, expanding its range of services to information technology. Established 10 years ago, Perftech currently employs 60 IT experts. The company has developed a comprehensive range of internet services since 1995. 

 PRIVATISATION SIT 179.7 Billion to Fill the Privatisation Gap 

 The government passed a report on the covering of the privatisation gap on 15 July. The report specifies the volume of funds needed to cover the gap to be at SIT 179.7 billion. The amount was calculated on the assumption that at least three quarters of shareholders would use the option to exchange Privatisation Investment Fund shares for pension vouchers under the First Pension Fund Act. According to the government decision, the property to cover the privatisation gap, the difference between the value of privatisation vouchers and the property to be privatised, would be made available by 31 July 1991. 

 TRANSPORT Slovenia and Croatia Discuss Transport Corridors 

 Slovene Minister of Transport and Communications Anton Bergauer and his Croatian counterpart Zeljko Luzavec discussed, at a meeting on 14 July, the development of railway and road transport, chiefly from the aspect of the construction of corridors no. 5 and 10. Both sides were of the opinion that the railway connection between the Croatian capital, Zagreb, Slovenia's Maribor and Austria's Graz should be upgraded as part of corridor n. 5. as soon as possible. But while Slovenia would like to retain the connection via Zidani most, Croatia would prefer a shortcut via Pragersko. According to Bergauer, the countries will further discuss this option as it has not been considered by Slovenia at all. As to the construction of motorways, the ministers tried to harmonise their countries' interests; while Croatia would like to see the Slovene section Maribor - Ptuj - the border crossing Macelj built as soon as possible, the Slovene side has not yet included it in its national motorway programme. The programme is th refore to be changed next year and likely ratified in parliament in 2001. The route of a motorway linking Croatia's Rijeka and Italy's Trieste was also discussed. 

 Ljubljana Ring Complete by End-August 

 Ljubljana's eastern by-pass will open for traffic by the end of next month according to the Slovene Company for Motorways (DARS). Final works are currently underway on a 14-kilometer motorway section, including the Golovec tunnel, which will be the only two-tube three-lane tunnel in Slovenia. Over the six years of implementing the national programme (since January 1994), a total of 143.8 kilometers of roads have been built, and another 47.4 kilometers of two-and four-lane roads at to open for traffic by the end of the year. 

 ENERGY Power Consumption Up by 0.7 Pc in June 

 807.3 million KWH of electricity was spent in Slovenia in June, up by 0.7 percent year-on-year. Power consumption was higher in both direct users who took 170.1 million KWH from the network as well as in distribution 637.2 million KWH). 

 AGRICULTURE Nearly DM 40 Million to Help Agriculture 

 The National Assembly adopted, on 16 July, the bill on the intervention measures in agriculture in 1999. The law worth SIT 3.95 billion (DM 40 million) will help pig-breeders, milk producers and wheat and hops growers. Nearly SIT 2 billion will be allocated for easing the situation in the milk industry at various stages of production. Half a billion tolars will go to the pig-breeding industry, and just as much to hops producers. Approximately one billion will be allocated to wheat and rye producers. 

 REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT Parliament Endorses Bill on Balanced Development of Regions 

 The National Assembly adopted on 16 July a bill to encourage balanced development of Slovene regions, an umbrella act specifying the goals and principles of regional development, the allocation of state funds and the criteria required to qualify for state subsidies. Besides, the law defines which regions need a fresh developmental impetus. Under the law, the government will have to earmark at least 0.5 percent of GDP for balanced development of regions in the first year after the law takes effect. In the second year, however, the figure will have to total at least 1 percent of GDP. 

 Petrol's Initiative for Development of Lendava Region 

 Slovenia's oil company Petrol has launched activities to revive the region of Lendava, the northeasternmost part of Slovenia where an oil refinery in which Petrol has a 55 percent stake is located. The initiative group of the consortium in charge of drafting and later implementing a development strategy met on 16 July at Lendava Castle on the initiative of President of Petrol Management Board Janez Lotric and Mayor of Lendava Joze Kocon.The next meeting of the initiative committee is expected to be held this autumn. 

 STATISTICS Poor Foreign Trade Results Caused by Depression in the Balkans and Russia 

 Slovenia recorded a considerable deficit in trading with foreign countries in May, which was chiefly due to political and economic problems in the regions of ex-Yugoslavia and the former Soviet Union. Exports to the EU member states - the largest and most important market for Slovenia - have been on a steady increase, marking a rise of 3.1 percent in the first five months of 1999 over the same period last year. The preliminary data show a deficit of US$ 149.9 million in May, which is expected to rise further after the data is supplemented. Last May Slovenia's exports totalled US$ 708.8 million, down by 4.2 percent over May 1998, imports were up by 0.6 percent to US$ 858.7 million in the same period. 

 Average Nett Salary Totals DM 1060 in May The average nett salary totalled SIT 106,558 (around DM 1060) in May, up 0.4 percent from April and 8.4 percent from a year earlier. May gross salary stood at SIT 168,628 (DM 1680), a monthly rise of 0.1 percent and a yearly increase of 8.4 percent. In real terms, however, the average gross salary fell by 0.5 percent over April and rose by 3.9 percent from May 1998. In the January-to-May period, the average clear pay amounted to SIT 105.665 (DM 1050), a 8.3 percent rise from the same period last year.Average gross wages were up 8.5 percent to SIT 167,141 (DM 1670) in the same period. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE Share Prices at LSE Rising 

 Share prices at the Ljubljana Stock Exchange fell on Monday and Tuesday, but the trend reversed on Thursday and Friday, with the SBI share index closing the week at 1765.49 points, up 11.56 week-on-week. Also up was the BIO bond index which gained 0.61 points to close the week at 106.87 points. 

 EXCHANGE RATES Higher Exchange Rates of Foreign Currencies

 All major foreign currencies saw their exchange rates rise according to the Bank of Slovenia mean exchange rate over the past week. The Euro rose by SIT 0.3 to SIT 191.7, German mark added SIT 0.2 to SIT 99.9, and Swiss franc edged up by SIT 0.3 to SIT 121.7. Austrian schilling and Italian lira remained flat at SIT 14.2 and SIT 10.1 respectively. 

 (c) 1999 STA, Slovenska Tiskovna Agencija d.o.o.

title: Slovene c.bank to cut banks' euro selling rate.
text:
LJUBLJANA, July 15 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Thursday it would determine commercial banks' intervention euro selling rate at a maximum of 197.37 tolars from Monday, while the maximum mark selling rate was set at 100.91 tolars. 

 The central bank did not say at what rate it would be selling foreign exchange to commercial banks participating in the intervention. 

 The central bank did not explain the move but analysts said it was designed to boost the value of tolar against the euro and mark. 

 This week commercial banks were selling euros to companies at an average rate of some 197.43 tolars and about 100.94 tolars per mark. 

 ((Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from 20 through 26 March.
text:
Ljubljana, 28 March (STA) - The coalition leadership has eventually made a first move in privatising state banks and insurance companies. According to Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, the banks will be partially privatised within this year, while in the case of insurance companies, the coalition has agreed on the basic principle and the methods of their privatisation to be integrated in the bill awaiting third parliamentary reading. 

 At the end of last week the board of the Krsko Nuclear Power Plant gathered for their first meeting in the last eight months and adopted the 1999 business plan. The Croatian members were absent, but Croatian Economics Minister Nenad Porges hosted his Slovene counterpart Metod Dragonja. Although it is not at all clear how the story of TAM will end, a contract stating national economic interests in the purchase of TAM was initialled by the Ministry of Economic Activities, Slovene Development Corporation and the prospective buyer, MTI Evropa. Mobitel, the so far only GSM mobile service provider in Slovenia, got a rival last week after Simobil launched its operation. 

 Chronology: Monday/22 March - Crnomelj: Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek meets business representatives of Bela Krajina (south). Tuesday/23 March - Krsko: President Kucan visits the region of Posavje region and meets with business people there. Tuesday/23 March - The Hague: Minister of Economic Activities and Development Marjan Senjur begins a three-day visit to Holland. Tuesday/23 March - Ljubljana: the National Assembly passes acts on foreign currency transactions and immaterial securities. Wednesday/24 March - Ljubljana: a salaries policy agreement is signed. Friday/26 March - Zagreb: Economic ministers of Slovenia and Croatia, Metod Dragonja and Nenad Porges, meet. Friday/26 March - Krsko: The Krsko N-plant board holds its first session this year. 

 INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION Slovene and Croatian Economics Ministers Meet in Zagreb 

 The Slovene and Croatian economics ministers, Metod Dragonja and Nenad Porges, met in the Croatian capital on 26 March. Dragonja and Porges discuss ways of settling the outstanding issues regarding the jointly-owned Krsko nuclear plant. The meeting was agreed upon by Slovene Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and his Croatian counterpart Zlatko Matesa, who met on 12 March at Otocec. 

 Minister Senjur Visits Holland 

 Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur paid a working visit to the Netherlands from 23 to 25 March. He met with Dutch Economics Minister Annemarie Jorritsma and Minister of Foreign Trade Geritt Ybema and opened a business conference and a panel on business and investment possibilities in Slovenia. In 1998 bilateral trade amounted to US$ 367 million. 

 Slovenia's Trade with Yugoslavia Weakened 

 NATO airstrikes on Yugoslavia are expected to make Slovenia's trade with Serb and Montenegrin companies difficult. Nevertheless, economic cooperation between Slovenia and Yugoslavia has now been hampered for several years because the countries failed to reach an economic agreement. Approximately 10 Slovene companies have their branch offices in both Yugoslav republics, Serbia and Monte Negro, among which there are pharmaceuticals company Krka and white goods-producer Gorenje. Moreover, nearly one thousand Slovene companies cooperate with Yugoslav partners. The tourist industry is expected to be most severely affected by the escalation in the Balkans, mainly due to the closure of the airspace. Slovenia's exports to Yugoslavia totalled US$ 112.4 million in 1997, but fell to US$ 102.7 million in 1998. Imports from Yugoslavia rose by 60.6 percent to US$ 67.5 million in 1998 from 1997. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Slovenia's Central Bank Stops Intervening by Purchase Price 

 The Bank of Slovenia stopped intervening on foreign exchange markets by fixing a purchase price. Effective since 25 January, the intervention purchase price period ended on 23 March, the Slovene central bank said. 

 BANKS State-Owned Banks to be Privatised as Early as 1999 

 Government coalition leaders reached an agreement on the privatization of state-owned banks. A 35-percent stake in the state-owned banks is to be privatised as early as this year, of which 10 percent is to be earmarked for filling the privatisation gap, Prime Minster Janez Drnovsek told a press conference on Friday. The government would retain the rest of its bank capital. An agreement was also reached at the meeting with the governor of the Bank of Slovenia and Minister of Finance that all relevant institutions would seek to act in a coordinated fashion. 

 Dismissal Procedure in SKB banka Found to be Legal 

 Governor of the Bank of Slovenia France Arhar informed SKB banka the procedure to dismiss the chairman of the bank's board was not found to be legally incorrect in any way. The supervisory board of SKB banka will meet again on 2 April, when it is expected to appoint a new member of the management team. 

 Nova Ljubljana Bank (NLB) Acquires a 20 Percent Stake in Dolenjska Bank (DB) 

 Nova Ljubljanska Bank (NLB) acquired Monday a 20-percent holding in Dolenjska Bank (DB). Before that, NLB only had a 7.7-percent stake in DB. Its stake increased to 20 percent after it purchased 53,687 DB shares from two authorised investment companies, including Maksima 2 and Maksima 3. The Nova Kreditna banka Maribor bank (NKBM) is also interested in buying a stake in DB. Last December, the bank purchased a nearly 24-percent stake in DB. At last week's meeting with Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari, the leaderships of NLB and NKBM were urged to harmonise their further decision on this issue with an appropriate development strategy of the Slovene financial markets. It was agreed that both banks' supervisory boards would inform the finance ministry in future about the details of the transactions regarding the purchase of DB shares. Both NLB and NKBM are predominantly state-owned. NLB bought the DB shares at an average price of SIT 21,845 per share. 

 Dolenjska banka Increases its Profit by 17 Percent 

 Last year Dolenjska banka made a gross profit of SIT 657 million (US$ 3.8 million), an increase of 17 percent over 1997. The bank enhanced the volume of business by 20 percent, increasing total assets to SIT 77.5 billion (US$ 445 million) by the end of 1998. Deposits by companies and citizens were up by more than 25 percent (SIT 12.5 billion), while investments in non-banking sector, i.e. companies and citizens, increased by 54 percent (SIT 15.5 billion). Loans to legal entities were last year up by 97 percent, which means the bank has no problems in placing funds, Director Franci Borsan said in a news conference in Novo mesto (southeast) on Wednesday. Along with a rise in the volume of business on the domestic market, the bank recorded an increase in the amount of business with partners abroad. 

 Probanka Makes a Gross Profit of SIT 460 Million 

 The Maribor-based bank Probanka made a gross profit of SIT 460 million last year, achieving a 9.6-percent return on revalued capital. The volume of trade amounted to SIT 47 billion, an increase of 26 percent over 1997. The bank, which holds a 1.5-percent share on the Slovene market, enhanced its assets by 16 percent or SIT 4.8 billion. 

 COMPANIES Contract to Sell TAM Initialled 

 A contract regulating national economic interests in the purchase of TAM, a vehicle-producer in receivership, in full was initialled Thursday by outgoing Economics Minister Metod Dragonja, President of the Slovene Development Corporation Bogdan Topic and Director of the Maribor-based MTI Evropa Martin Budna. The contract aims at specifying those parts of relations between the state and a potential buyer, MTI Evropa, that are not specified in the sales contract. These include, for instance, the preservation of production and its gradual increase, the preservation of the same number of jobs, investments in technological development and modernisation in the next five years. The initialled contact binds MTI Evropa to protect and develop all industrial property rights, particularly the trademark TAM.According to Dragonja, the contract will be signed and sent to the government only after MTI Evropa has paid a down-payment. 

 Slovene Ironworks Were Quite Successful in 1998 

 Manufacturing companies within the Slovene Ironworks concern incurred a nett loss of SIT 1.38 billion last year, which is only 16 percent of the amount of loss recorded in 1997. The rehabilitation programme, on the other hand, forecasted a loss of SIT 2.12 billion. Minor loss followed after the state and the state electricity company Eles furnished fresh capital. The 1998 operating loss, however, did not meet the target and amounted to 4.2 billion. The Slovene Ironworks concern recorded a nett loss of over SIT 10 billion, a decrease of four billion tolars over 1997. 

 Slovene Post Made a Loss Last Year 

 Despite a 90-percent increase in the volume of services, Slovene Post made a loss of SIT 651 million last year. Stamp prices in the internal post exchange cover only 50 percent of expenses. Slovene Post has therefore asked the government to raise the price of stamps by seven tolars. In case the government does not accept the proposal, the post will incur a loss of SIT 1.6 billion this year. 

 Elan Gets New Management Team Members 

 The supervisory board of the Begunje-based sports gear maker Elan appointed two new members of the company's management team on Wednesday. Ales Jerala will be in charge of the winter product line, while Davor Noc will take charge of the annual product range. The management nominated Edin Leho financial director of the Elan group. Elan's former management team was dismissed by the supervisory board at its session on 23 February. Elan's leadership and the trade union signed an agreement as part of the general saving measures on 26 March. The Zagreb-based Privredna banka, the majority shareholder, made further provision of liquidity funds conditional to strict austerity measures. 

 Intereuropa Enhances its Profit 

 Intereuropa, a Koper-based forwarder with 2,000 employed, made an income of SIT 11.356 billion last year, the unaudited and unconsolidated data show. The company thus increased its income by 5 percent from 1997. The 1998 nett profit amounted to SIT 1.369 billion and was by 2.3 percent higher than that in 1997. 

 Autocommerce Acquires a Majority Stake in Coming 

 Autocommerce signed a contract to acquire a majority stake in Coming. Last year the company turned over 34 million German marks. It is a leading company in the audio-visual sector in Slovenia and has a market share of 20 percent. 

 Hit Supervisory Board Discusses Investments 

 The supervisory board of Hit, a Nova Gorica-based hotel and casino owner, endorsed the 1999 investment plan draft at a session on 26 March. The company will need about SIT 5.6 billion for the whole investment cycle, the reconstruction of hotel Sabotin and investments in information technology included. 

 Cimos International AGM on Debt Enforcement 

 The AGM of Cimos International adopted several resolutions to grant a successful debt enforcement on 20 March. The shareholders passed a decision to increase the capital stock and a resolution to transform claims into ownership shares. Half of the debts will be written-off, 42 percent will be transformed in the company's capital, while eight percent (about SIT 5.7 billion) will be paid back by Cimos within ten years. 

 SLOVENE DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION Development Corporation Will Support Development Oriented Companies 

 The Slovene Development Corporation (SRD) will have a total of SIT 6.45 billion (US$ 37 million) at its disposal for this year. Seventy percent of the funds will be used for investments into development and the rest for investments in rescue operations. Apart from that fresh capital as financial assistance to companies, there are 8.5 billion tolars' worth of guarantees SRD will be able to grant its companies so that they can take loans with commercial banks, SRD Board Director Bogdan Topic told a news conference on Wednesday. The business plan in addition earmarks a write-off of SRD's old claims amounting to SIT 17 billion originating in the period from 1994 to 1996. 

 SRD to File Complaints against Smelt Intag's Former Management 

 Slovene Development Corporation, that is its company Gio, which holds a 100-percent stake in Smelt Intag, has drafted complaints against the former management team of Smelt Intag. Before filing them with the Swiss public prosecutor's office, Gio will complement them in view of material responsibility of the three-member board headed by Joze Zagar. The exact amount, which is said to exceed 10 million Swiss francs, is yet to be established by an independent Swiss auditor. 

 SALARIES Social Partners Sign a Deal on 1999-2001 Salaries Policy= 

 The government, trade unions and employers signed an agreement on salaries policy for the 1999-2001 period on 24 March. It defines basic principles and targets the social partners would like to achieve in salaries policy. The deal was signed only by two trade unions: the Association of Free Trade Unions of Slovenia (ZSSS) and KS 90 of Slovenia; as well as by the Employers' Association of Slovenia and chambers of commerce and trade. 

 TELECOMMUNICATIONS Simobil Launches Operations on GSM Market 

 Simobil, Slovenia's second GSM mobile telecommunications provider, launched its services on 25 March. According to the company, its prices are on the average 10 to 15 percent lower than those offered by the competition. The company expects to get at least a thousand subscribers on the first day of its operation and increase their number to at least 20,000 by the end of the year. The GSM telephone exchange in Ljubljana has a capacity of 250,000 subscribers. The company, in which Slovene stockholders hold a 75-percent share and Swedish GSM operator Telia the rest, plans to open a similar centre in Maribor before the end of the year, followed by centres in other Slovene towns. Simobil, which signed a concession contract with the government in October 1998, currently covers approximately 60 percent of Slovenia'a population and projects to reach a 90 percent covering by the end of the year. The company has signed contracts with over 50 providers worldwide. Slovenia's first network operator of the GSM mobile t lephony Mobitel, which has been on the GSM market since December 1995, has a 95-percent market share, while the rest five percent is held by Debitel, which uses Mobitel's network. Mobitel's share is expected to drop to 80 percent with the arrival of Simobil. 

 POWER INDUSTRY N-Plant's Board Passes 1999 Business Plan 

 This year's business plan of the Krsko Nuclear Power Plant was endorsed on Friday by the N-Plant's Slovene-Croatian board, meeting at Krsko without Croatian members. According to the decree with which the Slovene government transformed the N-plant into a public company, both state electricity companies, Slovenia's ELES and Croatia's HEP, have to sign a contract on power supply with the N-plant. Since HEP has not done it yet, it is unlikely to use Krsko-generated electricity this year, the board's chairman and general manager of ELES, Ivo Banic, told a news conference after the board's session Croatia's debt for the Krsko-generated power supplied last year amounts to SIT 1.572 billion (US$ 9 million). There is also SIT 1.453 billion for the plant's decommissioning. The debt has not changed since July 1998, when HEP stopped using electricity from Krsko. ELES sells electricity at a market price at home and abroad. 

 TRADE SHOWS A Show of Culinary Arts Opens in Ljubljana 

 A show of culinary arts featuring the food-procession industry opened in Ljubljana on Tuesday. Over 315 exhibitors from 17 countries were promoted at a surface of 8000 square meters. 

 Kranj Hosts an Agricultural Fair 

 The 38th international agriculture, food and forestry fair opened on 26 March to feature 612 exhibitors, as many as 117 of them from abroad. The exhibition grounds cover an area of 20,000 square metres. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE Shares Depreciate on Ljubljana SE 

 The SBI share index lost 46.48 point last week and closed at 1847.91 point. The BIO bond index depreciated by 0.96 point to 106.5 point. 

 EXCHANGE RATES Foreign Currencies Appreciate 

 All major foreign currencies appreciated last week according to the exchange rate of the Bank of Slovenia. The euro was up by SIT 0.21 to SIT 190.34, the U.S. dollar by SIT 1.87 to SIT 175.95 and the German mark by SIT 0.11 to SIT 97.32. The Austrian schilling appreciated by SIT 0.02 to SIT 13.83, 100 Italian liras by SIT 0.01 to SIT 9.83 and the Swiss franc by SIT 0.3 to SIT 119.3.

title: Slovenia central bank  ends  forex intervention .
text:
LJUBLJANA, March 23 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Tuesday that it would end intervention on the foreign exchange market as of Wednesday. 

 The bank started to intervene on January 25 when it set commercial bank buying rate for the euro at 189.52 tolars, which was later raised three times. 

 On March 15, the rate was last raised to 190.6 tolars for the euro from 190.3 tolars. 

 During the intervention the central bank was buying foreign exchange from chosen commercial banks at an undisclosed rate. 

 The central bank did not say why it decided to end the intervention. 

 Analysts said the intervention, which was designed to lower the value of the tolar against the euro, reached its target as the average commercial banks' rate for buying euros from companies rose to 190.55 tolars from 188.7 before the intervention. 

 ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).

text:
LJUBLJANA, March 15 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Monday it would raise commercial banks' intervention euro buying rate to 190.6 tolars from 190.3 tolars, effective Tuesday. 

 The central bank would buy foreign exchange from chosen commercial banks participating in the intervention, but did not disclose the rate. 

 The central bank did not explain the move but analysts said it was designed to lower the value of the tolar against the euro. 

 The central bank's previous intervention rate was effective from February 18, when it was raised from 190.11 tolars.

title: Weekly review of Slovene economy from 27 February through 5 March.
text:
Ljubljana, 6 March (STA) - The week was dominated by events in the business sector. Economics Minister Metod Dragonja stepped down after he was appointed vice chairman of the board in the pharmaceuticals maker Lek. Both Slovenia's pharmaceuticals manufacturers, Ljubljana's Lek and Novo mesto-based Krka last year reported lower profits than the year before. Several other companies announced their 1998 business results this week, the story about selling the car-maker TAM remained unended, and Minister of Ecomomic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur soothed public anxiety stressing there were no signs of recession. Another resounding notice this week was the recommendation of several commercial banks for ceiling interest rates, which caused the most concern in the Bank of Slovenia. 

 Chronology: Monday/1 March - Ljubljana: Inter-bank recommendation for ceiling deposit interest rates took effect. Monday/1 March - Begunje: Elan management dismissed. Monday/1 March - Maribor: Tam and MTI Europe did not sign the purchase contract. Monday/1 March - Ljubljana: Slovenia, Hungary signed contract to build railway line connecting the countries. Wednesday/3 March - Ljubljana: Economics Ministers Metod Dragonja stepped down. Wednesday/3 March - Ljubljana: Authorized investment companies (PID) filed motion to assess constitutionality of privatization conclusion act. 

 LEGISLATION Government Confirms Law on Budgets 

 The government passed and laid before Parliament for first reading the bill on national budgets on 4 March. Finance Ministry State Secretary Martin Cvikl said it was the key systemic piece of legislation for the area of public finances. 

 INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION Chambers of Commerce of Slovenia and Ukraine Sign Cooperation Agreement 

 The chambers of commerce of Slovenia and Ukraine signed the cooperation agreement on 2 March at a business conference in Ljubljana, attended by 13 Ukrainian and 40 Slovene companies. Both parties undertook in the agreement to promote economic cooperation between Slovenia and Ukraine. The representatives of both chambers underlined several other bilateral agreements, for instance investment protection and promotion agreement, should be signed. Slovene-Ukrainian trade has been up since 1992. In 1998 it totalled US$ 57.5 million and rose by US$ 1.5 million over 1997. Slovene exports to Ukraine amounted to US$ 42 million. Slovenia mostly exported pharmaceutical products and electrical devices. Nearly 200 Slovene companies have had business contacts with Ukraine; 19 of them have their branch offices or joint ventures there. 

 Slovene-Turkish Economic Relations Debated in Istanbul 

 A two-day seminar "Developing Slovene-Turkish Business Relations" intended to review economic relations between Slovenia and Turkey and devise ways for their consolidation started Thursday in Istanbul. The participants agreed that Slovene companies have good potentials for sales in Turkey's 60 million market. Slovenia will give a presentation of its economy in Turkey this August, the mixed economic commission is to sit in autumn, and the business council of both countries is to convene during the annual Regional Business Meeting Point at Bled. In 1998, bilateral trade toppled US$ 100 million for the first time. Slovene exports to Turkey amounted to US$ 57 million, recording a 74 percent rise y/y. Trade balance was positive for Slovenia for the first time after 1995. Exchange of services also increased last year. In 1997, exports of services amounted to US$ 6.9 million, while imports were at US$ 5.9 million. 

 A Line of Credit Opened Between Slovenia and Bosnian Federation 

 A cooperation agreement was reached in Sarajevo on Thursday by the Slovene Export Corporation (SID) and the Bosnian Federation Investment Bank. The credit line opened between both institutions should stimulate Slovene exports to the Bosnian Federation. It will create conditions under which Slovene exporters will be able to do business with the federation, Marko Plahuta, SID executive director of finances and guarantees, told journalists. SID expects that a great deal of Slovene exporters would be interested in taking out insurance policies through this line of credit. The credit line is worth is 25 million euros. 

 MACRO-ECONOMIC TRENDS Minister Senjur: No Signs of Recession 

 There are no signs of economic recession in Slovenia, Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur told press on Tuesday. He stressed most economic indicators had improved in 1998, and although lower growth is expected this year - it is to range between 3.5 and 4 percent - there are no signs of recession. Unemployment remains high and is not likely to fall until industry starts employing more people, while this year's inflation rate is not expected to exceed 3 percent before June.At a news conference on 2 March, Minister Senjur also spoke about duty free shops. He said transforming duty-free shops to retail shops would equal their termination since their specific locations and structure of demand by daily tourists from neighbouring countries and passengers in transit would only allow them to sell tobacco products. Introducing excise duties on 1 July, in turn, means gradual elimination of the duty-free element from Slovene duty-free shops and their termination in 2005. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Bank of Slovenia Will Intervene in Case of Lower Savings 

 The Bank of Slovenia will do all it can to maintain the current level of development and preserve relative stability of the national currency, the tolar, central bank governor Franc Arhar said Wednesday at a meeting with businessmen from the Gorenjsko region. The central bank will formulate its policy in accordance with the international situation. In case of negative international trends, the governor expects the national budget to be amended and hopes reason would dominate the wage policy. The central bank will intervene if domestic savings decrease, Arhar said. 

 BANKS Some Banks Lower Interest Rates 

 The Slovene Banks' Association (ZBS) has recently recommended that ZBS members reduce the highest deposit interest rates on domestic and foreign currency deposits after 1 March. It suggested that the highest yearly interest rates should range from 1 percent on call deposits to the base rate plus 4 percent (TOM+4) on over 2-year deposits. Although not binding, the ZBS recommendation took effect on Monday, the day when the inter-bank agreement on the highest deposit interest rates expired. The association recommended interest rates for foreign currency deposits that would be comparable to those in the European money market. 

 INSURANCE COMPANIES Generali SKB Insurance Company to Build Own Office Network in Slovenia 

 Generali SKB Insurance Company plans to set up its own office network, company leaders told a news conference Thursday presenting plans and problems the insurance agency is facing in the Slovene market. Generali SKB allocated over DM 10 million in the last two years to increase its presence in Slovenia, set up its own infrastructure and ensure smooth conduct of insurance businesses. Another DM 30-15 million of investments is to be made to the agency's office network over the next three years. 

 COMPANIES 

 Economics Ministers Dragonja Resigns to Take up Job in Lek Board of Managers 

 Incumbent Minister of Economics Metod Dragonja was appointed vice chairman of the board of managers of the pharmaceuticals maker Lek by the supervisory board at a meeting on Tuesday afternoon. Dragonja will be responsible for finances, economics and capital integration. The supervisory board also dismissed member of the board responsible for finance and capital markets, Igor Kusar. The dismissal was proposed by chairman of the board Andro Ocvirk. Minister Metod Dragonja offered his resignation to Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Wednesday. Drnovsek accepted his resignation. 

 Government Saving Cimos International 

 The government called for debt enforcement in the Koper-based automotive supplier Cimos International at its regular session on Thursday. In case debt enforcement is not agreed, Cimos would go bankrupt and about 2500 jobs within and outside the company would be lost, while the government could not have SIT 1.7 billion of its claims paid. The government agreed that its claims be transformed to an 8.6 percent stake in Cimos International during the debt enforcement procedure. It advised other para-state institutions which have over SIT 400 million of claims in Cimos to do likewise. 

 TAM and MTI Evropa Fail to Sign Sales Contract 

 Maribor-based MTI Evropa did not sign a sales contract to purchase TAM, a vehicle manufacturer in receivership, on Monday, 1 March, the deadline for signing the contract. According to Mirko Zagar, TAM trustee in bankruptcy, the contract has not been signed because MTI Evropa failed to pay a deposit of SIT 1.05 billion, one tenth of the contract's worth. The bankruptcy senate of the Maribor district court ruled on 15 January that TAM can be sold to MTI Europe for SIT 10.5 billion (about US$ 64.8 million). The deal had previously been approved by TAM's creditor committee. Further steps are to be decided upon by the bankruptcy senate of the Maribor district court and TAM's creditor committee. 

 Elan Management Dismissed Because of Mismanagement 

 Supervisory board of the sports-equipment manufacturer Elan dismissed members of the managing board on 1 March citing poor business results in recent years that have plunged the company in the red. The management has been unable either to stop or reverse the negative trends which led to massive losses that are expected to amount to eight million German marks at the end of the current business year which ends on 31 March. The supervisory board rejected the proposed business plan for the next season and has not yet appointed a new management. Elan's majority owner, the Croatian bank Privredna banka Zagreb, plans to sell its majority shareholding in the company, the new chairman of the managing board Vladimir Selebaj told a news conference on Monday. The bank has already made an offer to Slovene investors believing such a deal highly desirable for both sides as well as for Elan. No concrete bid has been made so far, which means all options are still open, including the one for management buy-out. 

 Comet Reports Lower Results 

 Comet last year made SIT 4.99 billion turnover, creating SIT 178.5 million profit, down 42.13 pc y/y. CEO Marjan Lorger named unfavourable exchange rate, lower sales and slightly higher taxes as the key reasons for lower results. 

 Kolinska Successful in 1998 

 Ljubljana-based food factory Kolinska met expectations in 1998. While it failed to carry out its plans in full, it did make nine percent more profits, which according to CEO Lojze Dezelak, is an achievement to be proud of. The company's net revenues amounted to SIT 9.5 billion, with net profits reaching SIT 792.5 million. This year, Kolinska will pay dividends for the fifth time after privatization. 

 Mercator Exceeds Plans 

 One of Slovenia's largest trade companies, Mercator made SIT 1.35 billion of net profit, about one quarter more than planned, according to unrevised and unconsolidated data. According to CEO Zoran Jankovic, the key reasons for the rise include a 9.7 percent increase in group-level revenues, lower costs at all levels and unification of procedures throughout the business system. Mercator plans to make SIT 1.58 billion profit this year. 

 Krka Reports Lower Net Profit 

 Krka pharmaceuticals reported SIT 4.16 billion (US$ 23.77m) net profit in 1998 according to unrevised and unconsolidated data, or 19.7 percent less than in 1997. Net profits from sales amounted to SIT 49.67 billion (US$ 283.8m), up 2.7 percent y/y. Operating profit was also up by as many as 76.2 percent from SIT 4.22 billion in 1997 to SIT 7.43 billion (US$ 42.45m). The increase is believed to be due to lower operating costs. Profit from regular operations decreased by 16.2 percent to 4.7 billion (US$ 26.85m). Compared to 1997, revenues from funding were down while outcomes from funding up. 

 TRANSPORT Renovation of Ivanje selo Motorway Viaduct to Continue 

 The left half of the Ivanje selo viaduct between Logatec and Unec on the Ljubljana-Koper motorway will be closed for traffic from 1 March to 31 July. Traffic will be directed to the other half of the viaduct until the tourist season starts. A third lane will be opened at the beginning of the tourist season. 

 Contract for Railway Construction between Slovenia and Hungary Signed 

 Slovene Railways signed a contract Monday with three Slovene building companies for the construction of the Slovene part of the railway connection with Hungary. Under the contract, the main contractor SCT Ljubljana and its two contractual partners Primorje Ajdovscina and GIZ Gradis Ljubljana have until the end of the year 2000 to build 24.5 kilometers of the new railway from the village of Puconci via Hodos to the national border. Slovene railways will take government-guaranteed loan from a consortium of Slovene banks to fund the SIT 11 billion (about US$ 64 million) project. 

 AGRICULTURE Hmezad Kmetijstvo Goes Bankrupt 

 The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Food and the Economics Ministry held several talks with banks to convince them to reprogram credits to Hmezad Kmetijstvo based in Zalec, central Slovenia. However, after banks set unacceptable conditions, the ministries agreed on 3 March that bankruptcy was the only way out for the highly indebted company. 

 Agriculture Ministry Says Situation in Pig Market will Improve 

 The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Food believes the intervention purchase of fattened pigs of Slovene origin would show its full effects next week so the situation in the market would improve rapidly. A total of 9510 fattened pigs were bought until 5 March, four days after the measure took effect. The ministry also said a protest rally of pig breeders, announced for next Wednesday, was not necessary. Imports of live pigs and pork halved in the last 14 days. At the same time, import prices from Austria rose slightly in the period. 

 TRADE SHOWS Fair Alps Adria - Home Winds Up 

 The fair Alps Adria - Home featuring building materials, furniture and heating equipment, winds up on Sunday afternoon. According to the estimations of the organizers, the number of visitors has met the expectations. The fair, which opened in Ljubljana on 23 February, featured about 400 exhibitors from 22 countries. Apart from the Slovene companies, companies from Austria, Croatia, India, Italy, Germany and Estonia were also directly present at the fair. 

 TOURISM All Elements for Tourism Promotion Act Ready 

 The Ministry of Small Business and Tourism drafted all subordinate acts for the Tourism Promotion Act and public tenders for tourism for 1999 until the set deadline, the ministry said at a news conference on 2 March, given together with the Centre for the Promotion of Tourism. Minister Janko Razgorsek also announced that the government would grant seven concession for organizing games of chance by the end of the week. Hit Nova Gorica is to get five concessions and Casino Portoroz two. 

 STATISTICS 92.1 Million Passengers in Slovenia in 1998 

 92.1 million passengers crossed Slovene borders in 1998, down 12.5 percent over 1997. The number of Passengers increased by 2.9 percent m/m in December. The figure was down 11.9 percent over December 1997. 

 February's Factory-gate Prices Down from January 

 Factory-gate prices fell 0.1 percent in February from January, according to preliminary data released by the national statistical office. However, a rise of 2 percent was recorded in comparison with February 1998. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE LSE: Lower Share Prices 

 Most shares at the Ljubljana Stock Exchange were down this week. A total of 16 shares saw their prices sink, bringing the SBI index down 46.69 points to 1888.31 points. Conversely, the bond index BIO gained 1.02 points to 107.08 points. 

 EXCHANGE RATES Higher Exchange Rates of Major Foreign Currencies

 US dollar gained SIT 3.1 to SIT 175.13, and Euro SIT 0.19 to SIT 189.73 this week according to the Bank of Slovenia mean exchange rate. Swiss franc was up SIT 0.01 to SIT 119.27, German mark added SIT 0.10 to SIT 97.01, and Italian lira (100) SIT 0.01 to SIT 9.80.
