title: Bank of  Slovenia  Will  Intervene  in Case of Lower Savings.
text:
Ljubljana, 3 March (STA) - The Bank of Slovenia will do all it can to maintain the current level of development and preserve relative stability of the national currency, the tolar, central bank governor Franc Arhar said Wednesday at a meeting with businessmen from the Gorenjsko region. 

 The central bank will formulate its policy in accordance with the international situation. In case of negative international trends, the governor expects the national budget to be amended and hopes reason would dominate the wage policy. The central bank will intervene if domestic savings decrease, Arhar said. 

 The governor rejected complaints by exporters who argued that money was pouring to importers because of the existing exchange rate policy. He said there was stronger need for a good, and consequently more expensive, monetary policy in smaller economies. I hope managers also voice their demands in bank supervisory boards while making plans for the next few years. As opposed to real economy, banks are specific. Companies can get overindebted and close down, banks can't, Arhar said. 

 Slovene banks granted SIT 240 billion of loans last year, nearly two times more than the year before. In consequence, Arhar said, this meant higher risks, but about 90 percent of the total are still good loans, which is a high figure compared to other countries in transition. The governor also pointed out the possibility of raising funds without financial agencies. There are quite a few sound companies in Slovenia that could issue bonds. Because of this the banks will need to lower their margins and consider mergers in order to remain competitive. Mergers and other forms of integration should not lead to renewed monopolies but make fewer banks more competitive, Arhar said. 

 Speaking of the changes made last year, Arhar listed lower inflation and decreasing real interest rates. Also, banking legislation was amended to liberalize capital flows and allow new treatment of risks involved in changing deposit insurances. 

 The governor stressed Slovenia should deal with the value added tax as soon as possible. He added that no near price rises are expected until June. On the contrary, prices might go down in the period. Slovenia will not change its inflation target because of VAT's introduction in June, Arhar said. 

 (c) 1999 STA, Slovenska Tiskovna Agencija d.o.o.

title: Bank of Slovenia raises banks' euro buying rate.
text:
LJUBLJANA, Feb 17 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Wednesday it would raise commercial banks' intervention euro buying rate to 190.3 tolars from 190.11 tolars, effective from Thursday. 

 The central bank would buy foreign exchange from chosen commercial banks participating in the intervention, but did not disclose the rate. 

 The central bank did not explain the move but analysts said its purpose was to depress the value of the tolar against the euro. 

 The central bank's previous intervention rate was effective from February 2, when it was raised from 188.7 tolars. 

 ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1999.

title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from 30 January through 5 February.
text:
Ljubljana, 7 February (STA) - Slovenia's becoming an associate member of the EU on 1 February brought no major change to the Slovene economy as the Interim Accord had been in force since 1997. Major changes, however, will apply to the field of finances. The Europe Accord enables EU banks to found its branch offices in Slovenia and relaxes the inflow of foreign loans. Customs for trading with the 15-nation bloc will be completely abolished in 2001 but Slovene insurance companies will have a four-year transition period to get ready for the advent of foreign competition. 

 While speculations about a merger of Slovene and Croatian pharmaceutical companies, Lek and Pliva, marked the past week, a Slovene-Croatian meeting took place to discuss the future of Slovenia-located ski factory Elan, whose major owner is a Croatian bank. 

 A new trade union association was set up in the past week, called Alternative. 

 Fed up with waiting for the government to supply the funds to fill the privatisation gap, the authorised investment companies (PIDs) decided to bring charges against the government. 

 Chronology: Monday/1 February - Ljubljana: Slovene and Belgian foreign ministers, Boris Frlec and Erik Derycke signed the agreement to protect and stimulate investment. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Changes to Fiduciary Accounts 

 A new regulation about fiduciary accounts took place on 1 February. The Bank of Slovenia has shortened from 7 to 4 years the period within which foreign investors are not allowed to sell Slovene securities. But the regulation applies only to the contracts signed after 1 February. When a foreign buyer purchases Slovene securities for less than 4 years s/he has to pay a fee set once every quarter by the central bank. The fee is currently 2.5 percent per quarter. Another change is that those purchases of shares that reach over a tenth of voting rights, that is a tenth of the initial capital of the company will be classified as direct investments. A record of them will not be kept any more on fiduciary accounts. 

 A decision to introduce fiduciary accounts was taken by the central bank in February 1997. 

 Bank of Slovenia Sets New Intervention Purchasing Exchange Rate 

 On 1 February the Bank of Slovenia set a new intervention purchasing exchange rate of SIT 190.11 for one euro. At the end of January this rate was set at SIT 189.52. 

 BANKS Leaderships of Two Banks Meet 

 The leaderships of Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor and Dolenjska Banka met on 2 February in Maribor, northeast, for the first time after the Bank of Slovenia gave approval to the purchase of a 24.05 percent stake in Dolenjska Banka. The banks discussed cooperation in the future. 

 Majority of Slovene Banks Not Prepared for Liberalisation 

 Moody's, a New York-based agency assessing investment conditions, has said in its report that most of the Slovene banks are insufficiently prepared for liberalisation of the banking sector. Slovene banks were said to be too small and burdened with too high operating costs, a limited number of products and services as well as with uncompleted restructuring of the Slovene economy. 

 TAXES Finance Minister on VAT 

 Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari said on 2 February it would be bad timing to abolish the basic interest rate TOM in 1999, when the value added tax is to be introduced. The minister added there was no need to postpone the introduction of VAT. Minister Gaspari stressed at the Chamber of Commerce management board session that the application of the nominal interest rate could lead to higher interest rates because of in-built inflation expectations. Previous inflation is included in the present base rate TOM. 

 ENTERPRISES Management Boards of Slovene and Croatian Pharmaceutical Companies Meet 

 The management boards of Lek and Pliva, Slovene and Croatian pharmaceutical companies, met in Ljubljana on 4 February to discuss the issue of both companies' cooperation, possibilities of joint projects and their cooperation on the Slovene and Croatian markets. Lek, which hosted the meeting, said the issue of capital integration was not addressed, with the exception of the issue of Pliva's stake in Lek. Representatives of the Croatian company said Pliva did not own any Lek shares. Capital integration may follow as a result of successful business cooperation, Lek stated in a press release. 

 Economics Minister Dragonja and a Croatian Bank Meet over Elan 

 Talks were held on 3 February about the Privredna Banka Zagreb's shares in Elan, a ski factory located in the Slovene town of Begunje. Slovene Economics Metod Dragonja and the chairman of the board of PBZ, Bozo Prko, also discussed some other issues regarding Elan's finances. Dragonja and Prko agreed to exchange information about a potential sell of the PBZ's stake in Elan and about some other financial issues. PBZ, the biggest Croatian bank, holds 77.25 percent of Elan's stock. It has been seeking for months a suitable bidder for Elan, a company it bought in December 1991 for just over 32 million Deutsche marks. 

 Mercator Supports 1999 Business Plan 

 The 1999 business plan envisaging a profit of SIT 1.58 billion was approved as well as investments of SIT 13 billion to capital goods for this year at a meeting of the supervisory board of Mercator, Slovenia's major trading company, on 4 February. Last year's results, which exceeded the company's plans, were on the agenda, too. The supervisory board also fully supported the Mercator's merger strategy. 

 Hit's Turnover Higher than in 1997 

 Hit's gross revenues totalled SIT 32.6 billion in 1998, a rise of 12 percent form a year earlier. With its gambling department accounting for almost SIT 29 billion, restaurant and hotel services made up SIT 3.6 billion of total gross revenues. The company paid taxes of nearly SIT 12.5 in 1998, up 16 percent from 1997. Last year's net profit is estimated at SIT 1.3 billion. A fall of 3 percent in visitors to Hit's facilities was recorded in 1997. 

 Sava Tyres Reduces Production Output 

 Mostly due to a fall in demand in the Middle East, Croatia and some parts of Europe, tyres for lorries in stock exceeded the demand at the end of 1998. Sava Tyres, whose 60-percent owner is U.S. Goodyear, has thus decided to reduce its tyre production in February and March. As a result some employees were asked to go on leave. 

 PRIVATISATION PIDs Bring Charges against the Government 

 Charges were brought on 5 February against the government by all those authorised investment companies (PIDs) that could not yet replace the privatisation vouchers (certificates) for property due to the unsettled issue of privatisation deficit. The PIDs insist that the government give them shares of and stakes in those enterprises that are owned by the government in exchange for privatisation vouchers. The Association of Management Companies, gathering PIDs, said PIDs were forced to sue the government in order to protect the interests of shareholders after the government had failed to provide state funds to fill the privatisation gap. 

 TRADE UNIONS Fifth Trade Union Association Founded in Slovenia 

 Eight trade unions founded on 1 February a new Slovene trade union association called Alternative. It currently has 8000 members. Its President Slavko Kmetic announced Alternative would become the second largest trade union association in Slovenia, (the largest is The Association of Free Trade Unions of Slovenia) after it is to gain members from all over the country. Membership of over 20,000 is expected. 

 TELECOMMUNICATIONS Digitel Wins a Case against a Government Decision 

 The Supreme Court ruled on 1 February that the government decision taken on 11 June 1998 to grant a GSM concession to Simobil and not to Digitel should be done away with. The court said the government decision contained no reasons about the factors that were deciding for the decision taken. The government will appeal against the ruling within 15 days. Nevertheless, the ruling brings no change to the appointment of Simobil as second GSM mobile telephony concessionaire, Simobil said, adding the concession contract with the government has been reached and is valid. The management team of Digitel said in a press release that the ruling had proved the government violated international public tender procedures. On 11 June 1998 the government chose Simobil second GSM concessionaire. The company was recommended by the government expert commission. From among Simobil and Digitel, which applied for public tender to be given concession to use radio-frequency specter to provide GSM services in Slovenia, the expert c mmission had chosen Simobil, saying its offer was more appropriate than that of Digitel as regards expert standards and criteria in the submitted documentation. 

 Simobil Starts Marketings it Services on 25 March 

 At the launch of Simobil's GSM mobile telephony services on 25 March the signal will cover 60 percent of the Slovene population but is expected to increase to 90 percent by the end of 1999. 80 million Deutsche marks have already been invested to the construction of infrastructure and to the concession fee. Additional 50 million Deutsche marks will be invested this year. While Simobil-provided GSM services will be cheaper than Mobitel's, an immediate and sharp drop in prices could not to expected. Mobitel is the other mobile telephony operator in Slovenia providing the service at the frequency of 900 Mhz. Simobil will shortly reach a contract on a syndicated loan of 70 million Deutsche with a consortium of Slovene banks. 

 AGRICULTURE Decree on Financial Interventions in Agriculture 

 SIT 16 billion will be allocated as financial assistance in order to preserve and develop agriculture and food production in 1999. A decree to that effect was issued on 4 February by the government. 

 ADVERTISING Advertising in the Slovene Media Turns Over DM 338 Million in 1998 

 Advertising in the Slovene media last year accounted for revenues worth almost 338 million Deutsche marks, of which 56 percent was turned over by television stations, 18 percent by papers and magazines, 14 percent by dailies and 4 percent by advertising posters. As the radio stations were excluded from the advertising research carried out by the Institute for Media Research it has only been estimated that 8 percent of the revenues belonged to radio stations. A rise of 50 percent in total gross advertising revenues was thus recorded in 1998 from 1997. 

 STATISTICS Factory-gate Prices of Goods Unchanged in January 

 Prices of manufactured goods remained unchanged in January form December, but rose by 2.4 percent from a year earlier. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE SBI Index Rises 

 Most shares on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange closed the past week at similar prices like a week earlier. With 16 shares up and 9 down, the SBI index rose by 14.19 points to 1901.06 points. The BIO index also was up 0.21 point to 110.52 points. 

 As of 1 February the Ljubljana Stock Exchange started publishing the PIX index about the shares of authorised investment companies (PIDs). PIX lost 5.86 points to 1089.61 points in the last week. 

 Foreign Portfolio Investment in January 

 Foreigners' sells of securities on the stock market totalled 7 million Deutsche marks net in January. 71 percent of all deals were concluded on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange. Net deals were at 2.2 million Deutsche marks until 15 January. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE Foreign Currencies Up 

 Major foreign currencies rose in the past week according to the mean rate of the Bank of Slovenia. The euro gained SIT 0.16 to SIT 188.98, the Deutsche mark SIT 0.08 to SIT 98.63, the U.S. dollar SIT 1.17 to SIT 167.05, the Austrian schilling SIT 0.01 to SIT 13.73, 100 Italian liras SIT 0.01 to SIT 9.76 and the Swiss franc SIT 1.12 to SIT 118.19.

title: Bank of Slovenia raises euro buying rate.
text:
LJUBLJANA, Feb 1 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Monday it would raise commercial banks' intervention euro buying rate to 190.11 tolars from 189.52 tolars, effective from Tuesday. 

 It said the central bank would buy foreign exchange from chosen commercial banks participating in the intervention, but did not disclose the rate. 

 The central bank did not explain the move but analysts said it was designed to depress the value of the tolar against the euro. 

 Prior to the central bank's first intervention on January 27, commercial banks were buying euros from companies at an average rate of 188.7 tolars. 

 ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Review of Slovene Economy from 23 through 29 January.
text:
Ljubljana, 31 January (STA) - Decisions taken at the last session of the Bank of Slovenia (BS) Council were presented by Governor of the BS France Arhar. The Council passed changes to the fiduciary account regime for portfolio foreign investments and to the payments of tolar deposits on financial loans taken abroad. It also adopted the objectives of the monetary policy for 1999, which include the 16 to 24 percent growth rate of the M3 monetary aggregate. The bank Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor was given a go-ahead on the purchase of 24.05-percent stake in the Dolenjska Banka bank. 

 The government unanimously refused to issue a permit for Mercator's purchase of Emona Merkur's 170,325 common registered shares. The decision was taken after basic guidelines for the national development strategy had been considered. Dissatisfied with the government decision, the Mercator management team decided Friday to start administrative proceedings at the Supreme Court. 

 Consumer prices have increased by 1 percent in January, putting the January inflation rate at 1 percent. A year-to-year rise in consumer prices is 6.1 percent. 

 Chronology: Monday/25 January - Singapore: Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur starts two-day visit to Singapore. Tuesday/26 January - Ljubljana: Minister of Labour Anton Rop visited by Panagoitis Roumeliotis, the coordinator of the EU's regional initiative for stability and good neighbourly relations in Southeastern Europe (The Royaumont initiative). 

 INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS Minister Senjur in Singapore 

 Slovene Minister for Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur met during his official visit to Singapore with Foreign Minister Jayaumar on Tuesday. The ministers discussed the Asian financial crisis and IMF assistance to the region. Minister Senjur briefed the Singaporean official about the measures the Slovene central bank had recently introduced to prevent the free flow of 'hot capital'. Senjur said the geopolitical position of Slovenia was an important meeting point enabling cooperation not only with Slovenia's neighbours but also with other Central and Eastern European partners. 

 Slovenia and U.S. for Closer Economic Cooperation 

 A seminar How to Do Business with the United States was organized in Ljubljana Thursday by the Slovene Chamber of Commerce (GZS). U.S. Ambassador to Slovenia Nancy Halliday Ely-Raphael said relations between Slovenia and the U.S. were good but there was still enough room for closer economic cooperation. Participants in the seminar were of the opinion that several bilateral agreements should be concluded in order to strengthen the cooperation in economy. In addition, Slovene companies could benefit more from the contacts established by the Slovenes living in the U.S. 

 The trade exchange with the U.S. accounts for just 5 percent of the total Slovenia's foreign exchange. In 1997 Slovenia's exports to the U.S. totalled US$ 243 million, while the imports from there amounted to US$ 284 million. 

 FINANCES Bank of Slovenia Introduces Several Changes 

 Governor of the Bank of Slovenia France Arhar presented Monday the decisions taken by the BS Council. The Council has adopted the objectives of the monetary policy for 1999, which include the 16 to 24 percent growth rate of the M3 monetary aggregate. The M3 rose by 20.2 percent last year, mainly due to domestic crediting. 

 The Council also passed changes to the fiduciary account regime for portfolio foreign investments and to the deposits in tolars to be paid for financial loans taken abroad. The first change means shortening of the seven-year period to four years during which a foreign holder of Slovene shares is obliged not to sell them. The other decision will soften borrowings abroad because a deposit in Slovene tolars worth 40 percent of the loan will not be required any more. It will be reduced and should range from 0 to 30 percent. Both measures take effect on 1 February. 

 Bank of Slovenia Chooses Banks for Intervention Buying 

 The central bank decided Tuesday that four Slovene banks, namely Dolenjska Banka, Abanka, Nova Ljubljanska Banka and SKB Banka will be obliged to purchase foreign currencies at the intervention exchange rate of SIT 189.52 for 1 euro. 

 COMPANIES Sales Contract for TAM Initialled 

 The sales contract of TAM, a Maribor-based vehicle producer in receivership, was initialled Friday by official receiver Mirko Zagar, Buyer of TAM John Eapen, Director of MTI Evropa Martin Buden and lawyer Pavel Pensa. SIT 10.5 billion for TAM has to be paid within 6 months. Only then the right to property will be transferred to the buyer. 

 Sava Tires Manufactures Over 5 Million Tires 

 Sava Tires, a Kranj-sitted company jointly owned by concern Goodyear (60) and the Sava joint-stock company (40), produced over 5 million tires last year and thus fully met its business plan. Sava Tires employes over 1700 workers. Its plan is to produce almost 5.5 million tires in 1999. 

 Jewellry Manufacturer Sold to AL Inzeniring 

 The Zlatarna Celje joint-stock company in receivership will be sold to AL Inzeniring, a Ljubljana-based company, for SIT 296 million, the bankruptcy senate of the Celje District Court decided at the beginning of the week. Following two failed auctions, a public invitation for tenders was issued at the end of last year with the opening price of SIT 291.6 million, that is 67.5 percent of the company's value. Two tenders arrived and AL Inzeniring was chosen after its programme and financial scheme were assessed as more favourable. 

 MERGERS Government Opposes Mercator's Bid to Take Emona Merkur Over 

 The government unanimously refused Thursday to issue a permit for Mercator's purchase of Emona Merkur's 170,325 common registered shares. The decision was taken after basic guidelines for the national development strategy had been considered. By worsening the economic situation of Slovenia as a whole as well as of the regions in which Emona Merkur is present, the takeover resulting from such a purchase would have a negative impact on the development of the Slovene food retailers in the long run. Dissatisfied with the government decision, the Mercator management team decided Friday to start administrative proceedings at the Supreme Court. 

 Shareholders of Kranj-based Trading Company Vote for "Triplet" 

 Shareholders of Zivila Kranj, a Slovene chain of supermarkets, decided on Friday to merge with two Slovene rivals, namely Emona Merkur and Emona Obala into a new company called Emona Zivila. 99.8 percent of the shareholders voted for the merger. 

 Trading Companies Zivila and Mercator Fighting for Loka 

 Zivila Kranj issued a bid to buy shares of its Skofja Loka-based rival Loka. Zivila will be purchasing Loka shares until 22 February. The bid will only be successful if 46 percent of Loka shares are bought. Having signed a letter of intent about a friendly takeover with Mercator last September, Loka opposes a Zivila takeover. 

 TOURISM Slovenia Recorded One-Percent Decline in Tourists in 1998 

 Slovene tourist resorts were visited by 1,797,217 tourists in 1998, recording a year-on-year decline of one percent. The first statistical data on the turnover in the Slovene tourist industry show the number of tourists was up by 4 percent to 103,174 last December from December 1997. Slovenia recorded a considerable decrease in the number of domestic tourists last year, while the number of foreign visitors remained on the level of 1997. The number of domestic visitors was down by 3 percent to 821,267, while the number of foreign tourists remained unchanged at 975,950. Between January and December 1998, domestic guests allowed for 3,229,061 tourist nights and foreign for 3,061,164 nights. The figures were down by two and one percent, respectively. 

 Slovene Tourism Promoted Abroad 

 Slovenia participated for the first time at the Holiday World Experience in Dublin from 21 through 24 January. The promotion was organized by the Slovene Tourist Board (CPTS), air carrier Adria Airways and the Globtur travel agency in cooperation with Crystal Holidays of Great Britain. The CPTS believes Ireland is an interesting market for the Slovene tourist industry, especially after Adria has introduced regular flights between Ljubljana and Dublin. The most favourite Slovene destination of British and Irish tourists is Alpine lakes and the mountains. The Slovene tourist industry is currently promoted also at the IRU fair in Austria's Linz as well as at a number of penal discussions promoting Europe in U.S. towns. The latter promotion is part of activities of the European Tourist Commission. 

 STATISTICS January's Inflation Totals 1 Percent 

 Consumer prices have increased by 1 percent in January, putting the January inflation rate at 1 percent. A year-to-year rise in consumer prices is 6.1 percent.The National Statistical Office has said the sharpest increase was recorded in prices of food and nonalcoholic drinks (2.7) and in prices of communications services (1.6); the latter were up mostly due to a price rise in some postal services (6.7416000n average). 

 Volume of Industrial Production Up 3.7 Percent in 1998 

 The manufacturing sector increased the volume of its production by 3.7 percent last year from a year earlier, the National Office of Statistics has said. At the end of 1998 the growth of productivity in industrial companies exceeded the growth in 1997 by 5.4 percent as a result of reduction in workers and increase in production in 1998. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE Shares of Pharmaceuticals Companies in the Lead 

 The last week saw a 4.6 percent rise in the SBI index, which closed the week at 1886.87 points after gaining 83.51 points. The BIO index edged up 2.64 points to 110.31 points. Fifteen shares were up and twelve down in the Friday-to-Friday period. Major rises were recorded in the shares of two rivals in the pharmaceutical industry. Gaining 14.4 percent, Lek closed the week at SIT 44,284, and Krka, gaining 12.8 percent, reached SIT 28,864 on Friday. 

 EXCHANGE RATES No Major Changes 

 In the past week the euro increased by SIT 0.07 to SIT 188.81 and the U.S. dollar by SIT 2.76 to SIT 165.87 according to the mean exchange rate of the Bank of Slovenia. Gaining SIT 0.03 to SIT SIT 96.54, another foreign currency on the rising side was the Deutsche mark. The Swiss franc, on the other hand, lost SIT 0,80 to SIT 117.06. Both the Austrian schilling and Italian lira remained unchanged. One schilling cost SIT 13.72 and 100 liras SIT 9.75. 

 (c) 1999 STA, Slovenska Tiskovna Agencija d.o.o.

title: Weekly Review of Slovenia's Economy from 20 through 26 September.
text:
Ljubljana, 27 September (STA) - After hard negotiations Minister of Economic Activities Metod Dragonja and Board Director of the Petrol oil company Janez Lotric signed a contract for the Nafta Lendava refinery on 24 September. It provides conditions for the short-term operation of the refinery. It determines the rights and obligations of both owners - Petrol has a 55-percent stake in Nafta Lendava, while the rest is owned by the state - until 30 August next year. The state will stand surety for Nafta Lendava to take a loan of SIT 500 million (US$ 3 million) to start the production. To subsidize Nafta Lendava's loss from day-to-day operations the state is to earmark up to SIT 65 million per month. 

 The state pledged to provide current assets of SIT 500 million by means of a special contract binding the Commodity Reserves Fund to buy oil, its derivatives or tanks from Nafta. Last week the government in addition passed a decree abolishing the eco tax on fuel oil of domestic production, while the state will ensure Nafta the supply of natural gas at a price enabling the refinery to manufacture methanol at a competitive price. Petrol pledged to supply 25,000 tons of crude oil to Nafta each month. 

 Both contractors agreed not to burden Nafta with the costs resulting from the financing of old liabilities until the end of August 1999. They also expressed readiness to change the claims - Petrol's amount to about two billion tolars and those of the state to SIT 3.5 billion - to the company's capital stock. 

 CHRONOLOGY 

 Wednesday/23 September - Brdo pri Kranju: Government started debate on the 1999 draft budget. Wednesday/23 September - Maribor: Three-day 1st Slovene Congress Transport, Traffic, Logistics, with international attendance was opened. Thursday/24 September - Ljubljana: Health care trade unions, the Health Care Chamber and the Ministry of Health signed an agreement on the rider to the Collective Agreement for health care and an accord on the measures to improve the organization and quality of health care. Friday/25 September - Ljubljana: The Slovene Railway Union called a six-hour warning strike for 8 October at the Ljubljana-Zalog and Celje-Tovorna shunting stations. 

 SLOVENIA - EUROPEAN UNION Slovenia At Multilateral Screening for Agriculture 

 Slovenia attended on 21 and 22 September the multilateral screening for the agriculture section covering fruit and vegetable. According to delegation leader, Agriculture Ministry State Secretary Franc But, the meeting showed the screened area would not pose particular problems, but other agriculture areas, cereals in particular, are expected to prove more demanding. To align with the European Union, Slovenia will have to amend its legislation and, most importantly, set up appropriate institutions. Harmonization of Slovenia's with the EU legislation for fruit and vegetables will be examined in the bilateral screening next week, on 29 and 30 September. 

 Slovenia Attends Multilateral Screening for Customs Union 

 Slovenia's adjustment to EU rules for the customs union will require a lot of work to build up staff and appropriate institutions, primarily the customs service, Vojka Ravbar, state secretary in the Ministry of Economic Relations and Development, who headed the Slovene delegation at the two-day multilateral screening, said after the screening session on Thursday. She added an important task will be to adjust customs tariffs, which Slovenia plans to carry out gradually until its accession to the Union. Slovenia has a quality customs service, but it will need to continue investing in its development according to Ravbar. By joining the EU Slovenia will enter an area without internal borders that controls goods on entry or exit from the common area under a unified system. In that, Ravbar said, of particular importance will be the EU information system used to monitor incoming and outgoing goods. 

 EU: External Factors Influence Economic Situation in Slovenia 

 The recovery of EU economies had a positive influence on the macroeconomic situation in Slovenia, the European Commission said in its autumn report on the economic situation in EU candidates. A higher growth rate of Slovenia's GDP was chiefly a result of an increase in demand for Slovene exports in the EU. A low salary growth rate, however, made home demand rather weak. As external factors brought about a higher growth rate of GDP, the European Commission stressed the need for reforms that would improve public finances, facilitate rehabilitation of companies and the financial sector, and resulted further privatisation of state-owned companies. 

 NATIONAL BUDGET Government Opens Budget Debate 

 The government started the debate on the 1999 draft budget bill during its regular session at Brdo pri Kranju on Wednesday. The key goal of the government's fiscal-budgetary policy in 1999 is a maximum public finance deficit of less than one percent GDP, Premier Janez Drnovsek said at the session. The draft budget proposes maximum government expenditure of SIT 933 billion, up SIT 63 billion from the 1998 budget. Nominal growth of government expenditure is planned not to exceed 7 percent. On the income side, the budget plans SIT 900 billion of revenues. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Central Bank's Council Expects Balanced 1999 Budget 

 Dealing with monetary and economic trends at home and abroad, the Council of the Bank of Slovenia established at its latest session that the recent events on world markets announced a possible deterioration of the situation in some large parts of the world, for which reason the period of favourable export demand could change very quickly for Slovenia. This can have a negative effect on Slovenia's further economic growth, the council of Slovenia's central bank assessed. In order that the process of stabilization and the introduction of necessary structural reforms should continue successfully, the council expects the government and the parliament to balance the 1999 national budget and to ensure budgetary expenses do not increase in real terms. 

Central Bank's Intervention on Foreign Money Markets Ends 

 Following the resolution of the governor of the Bank of Slovenia and in agreement with the 5th item of the bid for intervention on foreign money markets by means of intervention buying rate dating from 10 September, Slovenia's central bank announced the period of intervention ended on 21 September. The banks involved are not obliged to sustain the intervention buying rate as of Tuesday, 22 September, the Bank of Slovenia said. 

 CHAMBER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY OF SLOVENIA Chamber's Position on 1999 Budget Bill 

 The Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia (GZS) supports a development-oriented budget, but says the planned expenditure of SIT 930 billion is excessive. In its position on the 1999 draft budget, adopted on Thursday, the GZS also said the proposed budget deficit should not be spent on day-to-day expenditure. The position of exporters has already deteriorated because of the oncoming wave of global recession that resulted mainly from the crises in Russia, Asia and the Latin America. According to the Executive Committee, the government should pay special attention to downward trends in foreign markets and to deteriorating conditions for doing business of the Slovene industry, and take immediate action to improve business conditions primarily for exporters. 

 FAIRS Craftsmanship Fair Concludes 

 Having received about 210,000 visitors, the 31st International Craftsmanship Fair closed in Celje on 20 September. It featured 1,794 exhibitioners from 30 countries. The exhibition grounds extended over 55,000 square meters. 

 Furniture Fair Opens in Ljubljana 

 The 9th Ljubljana Furniture Fair was held from Tuesday through Sunday. The fair, presenting the latest products of furniture industry, was attended by 324 companies from 17 countries. All leading Slovene furniture manufacturers were present as well as a number of foreign producers. Furniture and other equipment for homes as well as for offices were exhibited at the fair. 

 First Show of Tourism, Hotel Services and Gastronomy 

 The first international fair of tourism, hotel services and gastronomy, EXPO-TAG, opened in the Portoroz Marina on 24 September. Covering the area of 1,000 square meters, the show features 50 exhibitors from Slovenia and Italy. 

 COMPANIES Color Expects Lower Income This Year 

 Color, Medvode-based chemical industry, recorded sales revenue of SIT 3.3 billion in the first six months of this year. The overall profit amounted to SIT 211 million. Color sells 28 percent of its production to the former Soviet Union countries. General Manager Bojan Dolar said the company would not fulfill its plans by the end of the year. The deviation from the envisaged results will depend upon further developments in Russia, but the profit will be lower than expected. 

 Sava Kranj Records Increase in Sales 

 Sava of Kranj turned over SIT 17 billion in the first half-year, an increase of 5.2 percent over the same period last year. The volume of production was up by 3.7 percent in the period. According to the consolidated profit and loss account, the half-year net profit of the pneumatics producer amounted to SIT 560 million, 42.4 percent up from the same period last year. Sava exports most of its production, with the share of exports in overall sales surmounting 86 percent. 

 Droga Successful in Half-Year 

 Droga food industry recorded an income of SIT 5.9 billion in the first six months of this year. The nett profit amounted to SIT 357 million, five percent up from the same period last year. The Portoroz-based company looks upon its half-year operation as successful. According to Finance Director Assistant Ales Skraba, a nett profit of over a billion tolars is expected by the end of the year. The company's performance in the first half-year was strongly influenced by relatively high inflation in the first quarter and mild winter. 

 Gorenje Business Results in the First Half of 1998 

 President of Gorenje Joze Stanic estimates the company's business results in the first half of 1998 were good, although they could be better. In the first six months Gorenje's company Gospodinjski aparati (kitchen appliances) manufactured over one million appliances with the turnover totalling 324 million German mark, which is a 15-percent increase over the same period last year. The Gorenje management, however, was not satisfied with the net profit that was only seven million mark instead of the expected 14 million. Gorenje remains the biggest Slovene manufacturing company and Slovenia's most important net exporter. Recently the sales have been very good in Germany, France, Croatia, Austria, Denmark and Poland, while in Russia they have been, due to the crisis, worse than planned, Gorenje PR department announced. 

 Petrol Sells Less Oil Derivatives 

 The Petrol business group recorded a 12-percent fall in sales of oil derivatives in the first half of the year, which reduced its clear revenues by 11 percent in nominal terms in comparison with the January-to-June period 1997. A clear profit of nearly SIT 520 million is 28 percent lower from the same period last year. Return on equity fell to 4.8 percent at the annual level. Petrol has explained its poor business results with a fall in the consumption of oil in Slovenia, which was down 10 percent in the first half of the year after a long period of steady growth; as a result of measures taken by neighbouring countries much less oil derivatives were sold in the regions along the state borders (the so called oil tourism), where over a fourth of all Petrol petrol stations are based. 

 Kovinotehna Incurs a Loss in Half-Year 

 Kovinotehna, a Celje-based international trade company, incurred a loss of over SIT 358 million in the first half of 1998, while it had made a profit of SIT 11.2 million in the same period last year. The main reasons for bad performance are according to Board Director Saso Gerzina high extraordinary expenditures resulting from considerable write-offs and too large amount of tied-up current assets, especially stocks. Kovinotehna operation revenues amounted to SIT 17.4 billion in the first six months of this year, a 10-percent increase over the same period last year. Revenues from the operation of the Kovinotehna group totalled about SIT 21 billion, while the loss amounted to SIT 354 million. 

 Donit Filter to Expand Production with New Owner 

 The company Donit Filter, based in Medvode outside Ljubljana, registered as Filtrauto Slovenija Ltd. this summer after French Filtrauto bought it in June last year, allowing it to continue marketing its products under the Donit Filter brand name. Providing fresh capital upon purchase and transferring part of its production to Slovenia, the new owner is currently engaged in preparations for Filtrauto Slovenija to build a new production facility that would unite all production on one single location. The company this year also plans to start production of cockpit filters, next year it is to move all production to new premises, while in 2001 it plans to make SIT 3.2 billion (US$ 20 million) of turnover with the annual production of 9.1 billion filters, according to its director general Krajnc. The company is currently still in the red, with its losses in 1997 amounting to SIT 200 million (US$ 1.25 million). Director general Krajnc expects the business result to become positive after moving to the new factory. 

 Ormoz Sugar Factory Starts Production of Sugar 

 The Ormoz-based sugar factory is to start the processing of this year's sugar beet later this week. This year the factory in Ormoz, eastern Slovenia, is to buy 350,000 tons of sugar beet; in three months some 45,000 to 47,000 tons of sugar are to be made, depending on the contents of sugar in the beet. Last year the factory bought 288,000 tons of beet, making slightly less than 43,000 tons of sugar. Farmers tend to increase the production of sugar beet and by the year 2002 Slovenia should cover its needs - some 80,000 tons of sugar per year - with the domestic production. According to Dogsa, this would be a good basis for the definition of quota when entering the European Union, as the quotas are defined in accordance with the average production in five years' time.The Ormoz factory, employing 309 people, is owned by Dutch Consun (57-percent stake) and Italian Sucadria (25-percent stake). Last year's turnover totalled SIT 6.351 billion, while the net profit was SIT 89 million. This year both are to be increased, although the factory is facing problems due to high price of beet and low price of sugar. 

 SLOVENE RAILWAYS Slovene Railways Sign Contract to Purchase Pendolino Trains 

 Slovene Railways (SZ) and the Italian FiatFerroviaria company signed a contract of SIT 4.33 billion on Monday for the Slovene company to purchase three new Pendolino trains. The contract covers three trains, spare parts, a special maintaining equipment and the necessary documentation. To pay for the order, SZ will take a loan from a consortium of Slovene banks, for which the government has already issued a guarantee through passing a special law. The trains, whose maximum speed is 200 km/h, will be delivered in the middle of 2000, and will run between the towns of Ljubljana and Maribor. 

 SLOVENE IRONWORKS Gov't Examines Performance of Slovene Ironworks 

 The government examined the rehabilitation process of the Slovene Ironworks at its session of 24 September. According to State Secretary Boris Sustar, the Slovene Ironworks output was increasing both in terms of its size and value, although the company Acroni was lagging behind the rehabilitation plan. The Slovene Ironworks have cut the losses by half to SIT 1.3 billion in the first six months of this year. This marks an important step forward from last year, but it is still far from the objective set in the rehabilitation plan. The government believes the rehabilitation as well as the privatization processes should be accelerated, complementing it by internal management rationalization. According to Sustar, demand for thick stainless plates has already decreased because of the anti-dumping procedure against the Slovene Ironworks. 

 Expert Group Set up to Refute Allegations of Dumping 

 A group of domestic and foreign experts has been set up by the Slovene Ironworks and Acroni of Jesenice to refute the allegations about the dumping of stainless steel which moved the European Commission to launch an inquiry against Acroni. The Slovene Ironworks and Acroni see the complaint as a legitimate move in their competitors' struggle for the market. Last week the ironworks received a comprehensive and demanding questionnaire from the EU. They are determined to explain by means of appropriate answers that the sale of stainless steel was not a case of dumping. 

 Internal Distribution of Shares Begins in Ironworks 

 The management of the Slovene Ironworks decided, in agreement with the Privatization Act, that the internal distribution of shares to the employed and former employed in the companies of the concern start on 25 September. The distribution will conclude on 30 October. The beneficiaries - the employed, former employed and the retired - will be able to exchange their privatisation vouchers and receipts of unpaid salaries for shares. 

 TOURISM This Year's Tourist Season Successful 

 Minister of Small Business and Tourism Janko Razgorsek met heads of 36 largest hotel and health resort companies in Slovenia on 21 September. According to him, this year's season has been successful so far. By the end of August the foreign currency influx from hotel, health resort and casino services was by about 15 percent higher than in the same period last year. Sales of petrol and cigarets to foreign subjects, however, were down on account of measures taken by Italy and Austria, so the total of this year's foreign exchange influx from tourism will be lower than last year's. 

 Logo of Slovene Tourism on Adria Airways Aircraft 

 Five aircraft of Slovene air carrier Adria Airways will now carry the logo of Slovene tourism - the word Slovenia surrounded by flowers. Adria Airways last year brought to Slovenia some 44,000 foreign tourists, which is a 7-percent increase over the year 1997. Most tourists flew in from Germany, followed by Great Britain, Russia, Israel, Denmark, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Spain and Turkey. The increase is a consequence of cooperation between Adria and the Centre for Tourism Promotion - the centre's representatives namely often work in Adria's offices abroad. 

 TRAFFIC Contract Signed for the Reconstruction of Logatec-Robic Road 

 The national Direction for Roads signed a contract with four contractors on 24 September, launching the reconstruction of a 56-kilometer long section of the main road between Logatec and Robic. The contract amounts to SIT 1.468 billion. The project will be funded by the loan of the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development. 

 Slovene Truckers Need More Permits for the EU 

 The Ministry of Transport and Communications has responded to truck drivers' warnings of the lack of permits for international haulage. The ministry proposed that the Chamber of Commerce and Industry as well as the Chamber of Trade should have a more active role in the distribution of permits in the future. As the ministry established, permits for the EU countries are lacking most, while the situation is reversed in the case of East European countries. As far as Italy is concerned, only eight percent of 53,000 permits are used properly (in both directions), the ministry found. In the beginning of October the Slovene-Italian commission is expected to meet and the Slovene side will try to negotiate an increase in the quota of permits. It will in addition ask the Italian side to supply the information about the cases of fake permits detected with Slovene truck drivers so that the ministry will be able to start legal actions against the perpetrators. 

 STATISTICS Lower GDP Growth in Q2 

 Following a high, 6.5 percent growth rate in the first quarter of the year, GDP growth was much lower in the second quarter. Y/Y growth over Q2 1997 was 3.2 percent, while compared to Q1 1998 it was .5 percent. GDP growth in the first six months of 1998 over the same period last year was 4.8 percent. Compared to the second quarter of 1997, GDP growth was the highest, 5.8 percent, in the traffic, warehousing and communications sectors. Somewhat lower were the figures for financial services (5.6) and the processing sector (4.7). Basic industries recorded 3.7 percent annual growth, while service 2.6 percent growth. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE Shares Up on the Average 

 Prices of shares on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange increased on the average last week. The SBI share index gained 34.87 point and concluded the week at 1676.36 point. The BIO bond index was up too, by 1.12 point to SIT 105.42. 

 EXCHANGE RATES U.S. Dollar Down 

 The mean price of the U.S dollar was down by three tolars to SIT 157.25 in a week according to the Bank of Slovenia. The Swiss franc depreciated by SIT 0.6 to SIT 114.29, while other major foreign currencies did not change much: the German mark was up by SIT 0.04 to SIT 94.45, the Austrian schilling stayed put at SIT 13.42, as did 100 Italian liras at SIT 9.55.

title: Bank of  Slovenia  ends tolar rate  intervention .
text:
LJUBLJANA, Sept 22 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Tuesday it had concluded its tolar exchange rate intervention that began on September 14. 

 "From Tuesday, September 22, the chosen banks are no longer obliged to maintain the intervention exchange rate," the bank said in a statement. 

 From September 14, banks were buying foreign currency from companies at a rate of 94.7 tolars to the German mark, up from 94.4 tolars at the start of the month. 

 Analysts said the central bank had decided to intervene in order to slow the appreciation of the tolar. 

 Bank foreign currency buying rates from companies were at the start of September almost the same as those at the beginning of the year although consumer prices have risen 3.8 percent over the first eight months of 1998.

title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from 6 through 12 September.
text:
Ljubljana, 13 September (STA) - Following Croatia's comments on the government decree on the Krsko Nuclear Plant's reorganization into a public company, the Slovene side on Monday submitted its stands on the comments to Croatia. The document containing Croatian comments consists of 15 points that can be summarized in three demands: co-ownership with a 50-percent stake, consensus in decision-making and terms of payment and guarantee. After a thorough examination of all the points, the Slovene side could only consider a part of them, especially in the part where both partners shared the same views, but could not accept those whose adoption would disagree with Slovene legislation. 

 Current developments between electricity industries of Slovenia and Croatia were discussed by the Administrative Board of the Power Industry Association at its Tuesday session. Members of the body working within the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia (CCIS) were addressed by Ivo Banic, director of the Slovene electricity company ELES, and Alojz Kovse, state secretary for power industry. The Krsko N-plant operated at full capacity, achieving a 95.7-percent capacity utilization and generating 441,435 MWh of electricity. 

 Chronology: Tuesday/8 September - Ljubljana: the Council of the Bank of Slovenia adopts a decision to intervene on foreign money markets Wednesday/9 September - Nova Gorica: a contract signed to supply and assemble the equipment for the reconstruction of hydroelectric power plants on the lower Isonzo river Thursday/10 September - Ljubljana: the government and the Petrol oil company launch negotiations over Nafta refinery Thursday/10 September - Ljubljana: the government adopts a strategy of shoe industry restructuring Friday/11 September - Prague: CEFTA summit begins Friday/11 September - Celje: the 31st International Craftsmanship Fair opens 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Central Bank Council Decides for Intervention on Foreign Money Markets 

 The Council of the Bank of Slovenia discussed a banking bill and adopted several resolutions at a session on Tuesday. It passed a decree on the intervention on foreign money markets by means of an intervention buying rate. Banks chosen through tenders will buy foreign exchange at the rate SIT 94.7 for one German mark as of 14 September. The banks' rate for the purchase of foreign cash in exchange offices may not be lower than 0.2 percent in case of German marks or 0.4 percent in case of other foreign currencies. 

 GOVERNMENT Gov't and Petrol Negotiate on Nafta Refinery 

 Chairman of the Board of Petrol Janez Lotric and Minister of Economic Activities Metod Dragonja on Thursday began a new round of negotiations over the contents of a contract between the oil company and the government to re-start the Nafta Lendava refinery. On Friday working groups harmonized a draft contract, having negotiated compromise solutions in some points. These were discussed by Petrol Supervisory Board on the same day. In the talks the state insisted on it that Petrol secure crude oil supplies so that the refinery could start operating even this month. 

 Gov't Adopts Shoe Industry Restructuring Strategy 

 The government adopted a strategy of restructuring and jobs renewal in the shoe industry on Thursday. The strategy had been prepared by the Ministry of Labour, Family and Social Affairs in cooperation with the Ministry of Economic Activities. The document envisages certain financial investments, by the state as well as by individual companies, Labour Ministry State Secretary Zdenka Kovac told a news conference after the cabinet session. The total of required investments over the following years is estimated at SIT 14 billion. The state is to provide three to four billion tolars in the next five years. 

 INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC COOPERATION Slovenia Attends CEFTA Summit in Prague 

 A two-day meeting of Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) member countries' prime ministers began in the Czech capital on Friday. It gathered heads of governments of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Rumania, Slovakia, Slovenia and for the first time also Bulgaria. Addressing his counterparts, Slovene Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek made a special note of the signing of Additional Protocol No. VI to CEFTA last December. It stipulates liberalization of trade in agricultural products between Slovenia and CEFTA members. The seven CEFTA prime ministers on Friday signed a final declaration stressing CEFTA's contribution to the development and growth of trade among its member states as well as its contribution to a speedier accession to the European Union. 

 Chamber of Economy Delegation Visits Slovakia 

 A 23-strong Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia (CCIS) delegation led by CCIS Chairman Jozko Cuk started a three-day visit to Slovakia Tuesday, during which it held a business conference and several business meetings with Slovak partners in Bratislava, Nitra and Kosice, where representatives of 17 Slovene enterprises discussed concrete forms and possibilities for business cooperation. 

 Slovene Business Representatives also in Siberia 

 A Slovene economic delegation on Tuesday participated in a business conference in Tyumen, the capital of a west Siberian region of the same name, which the delegation visited led by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia (CCIS). The meeting was attended by ten representatives of Slovene companies and 46 Russian counterparts. 

 SLOVENE DEVELOPMENT COMPANY Restructuring Process Successful 

 The restructuring process in the enterprises Litostroj and Andria Mobil is getting on very well, and positive results have also been recorded in other companies run by the Slovene Development Company (SRD), SRD officials said in a news conference on Wednesday. SRD board of managers also presented the sale of Maribor's textiles manufacturer MTT, the activities concerning the Rogaska health resort and the acquisition of the 90 percent stake in the Goricane Paper Mill. SRD transformed part of its claims to a capital investment of DM 6 million, to provide easier access to bank loans to Goricane. At the end of July, SRD also bough the Austrian stake in the company, becoming the over 90 percent owner of the paper mill. SRD chairman of the board, Bogdan Topic also introduced a new member of the board, Barbara Kuerner Cad, a former economic court judge. 

 SLOVENE EXPORT CORPORATION Slovene Export Corporation, Hermes Sign Insurance Contract 

 The Slovene Export Corporation (SID) and Germany's exports-credit agency Hermes signed a joint insurance contract in Hamburg on Thursday. The contract, signed by SID chairman of the board Marjan Kramar and president of Hermes, Hans Janus, is intended to promote exports of Slovene and German enterprises by providing insurance and more favourable funding for joint export projects and investments in third countries. It will also joint actions by enterprises from both countries in third markets. 

 TOURISM Incomes from Tourism This Year Lower than Expected 

 Slovene tourism foreign currency influx in 1998 was lower than expected, secretary of Slovene Tourist Association Alojz Soster told a news conference on Monday. According to him, the expected proceeds in tourism amounting to US$ 2 billion will not be realized. Similar trends can be also seen in other European countries where tourism is developed, the main reason for this being journeys to the more distant and exotic places, which are getting cheaper. "We will be glad if the last year's proceeds amounting to slightly more than US$ 1.2 will be achieved," Alojz Soster explained. 

 AGRICULTURE Agriculture and Food Industry Association on Perspectives of Accession to the EU 

 A lively discussion on the opportunities of Slovenia's food industry in accession to the EU was conducted among Agriculture and Food Industry Association officials at the CCIS headquarters on Tuesday. The Slovene food industry is on the right path according to the EU report, there is nevertheless still much to be done, CCIS representatives maintained. Among the required measures, the EU report includes an increase in investments needed to improve on the industry's efficiency and especially restructuring and merging of Slovene food companies to increase their competitive power. 

 CEFTA Agreement of Little Benefit to Slovene Agriculture 

 The study on the Slovene agriculture and the CEFTA agreement, which was presented at the Zootechnical Department of the Biotechnical Faculty at Domzale on Monday, shows the Slovene agriculture has not profited much from the CEFTA agreement. It says the agreement has distinctive deficiencies and provides opportunities only to a limited number of branches. The agreement's hazards are so great that they endanger the basic strategic principles of development of the Slovene agriculture, also from the aspect of Slovenia's accession to the EU. The study claims Slovene farmers' incomes are very likely to decrease or, at the best, stay at the present level. 

 POWER INDUSTRY Nuclear Power in Central Europe Discussed at Catez 

 A regular annual international expert meeting of the Nuclear Expert Society of Slovenia (DJSS) was held at the Terme Catez health resort from Tuesday through Thursday. The meeting on 'Nuclear Energy in Central Europe' featured presentations of the latest achievements in the field of nuclear safety, papers on operational problems of research reactors and nuclear power plants as well as disposal of nuclear waste. The participants talked about the progress in the technical reconstruction of the Krsko Nuclear Power Plant in Thursday's round-table discussion. For the first time this year several papers focused on the use of nuclear methods in medicine, technics and industry. 

 Isonzo Hydroelectric Power Plants Sign Contract on Reconstruction 

 A contract on the supply and assembling of the equipment for the reconstruction of the Doblar II and Plave II hydroelectric power plants on the lower Isonzo River was signed on Wednesday in Nova Gorica (west) by representatives of Soske elektrarne of Nova Gorica, Rudis of Trbovlje, Litostroj of Ljubljana and Koncar of Croatia. The investment value of the equipment according to the contract is SIT 2.5 billion. Electrical generator sets of both power plants will have a joint capacity of 58.4 MW (Doblar 40 MW and Plave 18.4 MW). 

 TRANSPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS A By-Pass Opened at Ormoz 

 A 3.75 kilometer motorway by-pass around Ormoz, eastern Slovenia, that will ensure smooth and safe traffic in the region, was opened by the Minister of Transport and Communications on Friday. The Ormoz by-pass constitutes the first part of the new motorway from Slovenjska Bistrica via Ptuj to Ormoz, to be partially renovated or constructed until 2002 under the national motorway construction programme. The by-pass was built in 14 months by building companies GIZ Gradis and SCT Ljubljana together with Cestno podjetje Celje. The investment is worth SIT 1.4 billion (about US$ 8.5 million). 

 SMALL BUSINESS A Seminar on How to Promote Development of Small Business 

 The Faculty of Business and Economics in Maribor on Monday hosted a seminar on encouragements for a quicker development of small business in Slovenia organized by the Ministry of Small Business and Tourism. Minister Janko Razgorsek said assistance was most needed in companies' access to financial funds, business knowledge and experience, access to information, infrastructure, technology, innovation, development and internationalization of operation. 

 FAIRS Minister Razgorsek Opens 31st International Craftsmanship Fair 

 Minister of Small Business and Tourism Janko Razgorsek on Friday opened the 31st International Craftsmanship Fair (MOS), the second largest craftsmanship and business fair exhibition in Europe and one of the key business events in Slovenia. This year the fair, covering 55,000 square meters of exhibition surfaces, is attended by 1794 exhibitors from 30 countries. 

 COMPANIES New Lek-Bosnalijek Plant Opened in Sarajevo 

 Slovene President Milan Kucan and president of the Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic on Monday opened the renovated and modernized solid drug forms factory of the Bosnalijek corporation, in which the Slovene pharmaceuticals maker Lek is present with a US$ 1.5 million investment. In May this year Lek and Bosnalijek signed another contract for the equipment installation and technological installation worth 0.5 million D-marks. The works are scheduled to finish in October. 

 Slovene Ironworks Incur a Loss of SIT 1.6 billion in Seven Months 

 The Slovene Ironworks Group made SIT 1.6 billion of losses or SIT 400 more than expected in the first seven months of the year, with Acroni Jesenice accounting for the bulk of the loss of SIT 1.5 billion, chairman of the board, Miran Tasic told a news conference on Thursday. Tasic condemned the proposed anti-dumping procedure that was to be started against Acroni Jesenice by the European steel builders association Eurofer because of Acroni's exports of rolled steel plates. Tasic tackled also the issue of the ironworks' privatization and rehabilitation. General Manager of Acroni Vasilij Preseren met with European Commission representatives on Friday in an attempt to convince them that the allegations about dumping of stainless steel by the Slovene company were not grounded. 

 Simobil Increases Initial Capital by SIT 1.7 Billion 

 The management of Simobil, joint-stock company providing telecommunication services, passed a resolution to increase the initial capital by 1.7 billion from SIT 3 million to SIT 1.703 billion. The decision to increase the capital by shareholders' additional investments was adopted at the second general meeting of the company. 

 Union Brewery Awarded Gold Medals for Quality 

 Monde Selection, Brussels-based international institute of quality assessment, this year awarded gold medals for quality to six products of the Union brewery: beers Union and Union Pils, beer and lemon juice beverage Union Radler, ice tea Sola peach and red cranberry flavors and mineral water Zala. The latter was awarded a great gold medal. 

 STATISTICS Average Catering Prices remained Unchanged in August 

 Prices of catering in August 1998 on the average retained the level of a month before. Catering prices were up by 5.8 percent from December 1997 and up by eight percent from August 1997. 

 Exports above US$ 800 Million for the First Time in July 

 Slovene exports amounted to US$ 818.7 million in July and imports to 840.8 million. Trade deficit was US$ 22.1 million, while exports/imports ratio was 97.4 percent, up from July 1997 when trade deficit was at US$ 56.7 million and exports/imports coverage 93.1 percent, the National Statistical Office said. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE SBI Index Down Again 

 Fourteen shares depreciated and ten appreciated in stock quotations of the Ljubljana Stock exchange last week. The SBI share index lost 29.41 point and concluded the week at 1769.51 point. The BIO bonds index slid by 0.44 point to 104.90 point. 

 EXCHANGE RATES Most Major Foreign Currencies Depreciates 

 Apart from the Swiss franc and Austrian schilling, major foreign currencies depreciated last week according to the mean rate of the Bank of Slovenia. The franc was up by SIT 0.31 to SIT 115.07, while the schilling stayed put at SIT 13.41. The U.S. dollar was down by SIT 4.99 to SIT 159.47, the German mark by 0.01 to SIT 94.37 and 100 Italian liras by SIT 0.01 to SIT 9.55.

title: Slovenia  cenbank says to  intervene  on tolar market.
text:
LJUBLJANA, Sept 10 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Thursday it would begin tolar exchange rate intervention on Monday. 

 "From September 14 onwards the chosen banks will be buying foreign currency at a rate of 94.7 tolars to the German mark," the bank said in a statement. 

 Currently banks buy foreign currency from companies at a rate of about 94.4 tolars to the mark. 

 The bank did not say at what rate it would buy foreign exchange from the banks in question. 

 Analysts said the central bank decided to intervene in order to slow down the appreciation of the tolar. 

 Current bank foreign currency buying rates from companies are almost the same as those at the start of the year although consumer prices have risen 3.8 percent since the start of 1998. 

 ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).
