title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from 5 to 11 July.
text:
Ljubljana, 12 July (STA) - Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's economic college, which comprises ministers dealing with economic affairs, discussed Monday the analysis of economic trends in 1998 and a development projection for next two years, placing special emphasis on drafting the 1999-2000 national budget, basic macroeconomic projections and conditions in public finance. Based on the latest data, economic ministers again confirmed that positive economic trends in Slovenia continued. 

 The ministers also established that results of the spring report 1998 by the Institute for Macroeconomic Analyses and Development proved the government was staying firmly on course towards macroeconomic objectives and had this year achieved the set goals. About six percent higher economic growth than predicted in the beginning of the year was recorded in the first quarter of 1998. GDP growth is expected to at least topple four percent. 

 Chronology: Monday/6 July - Brussels: Slovenia with EU on economic priorities Wednesday/8 July - Ljubljana: Economic-Social Council passes grey economy prevention bill Wednesday/8 July - Ljubljana: Bank of Slovenia ends period of using intervention purchase exchange rate Wednesday/8 July - Ljubljana: Government passes regulation setting the procedure of closing tally accounts of privatisation voucher holders and the use of privatisation vouchers Thursday/9 July - Ljubljana: Government inter alia debates situation in the processing industry Friday/10 July - Potoroz: Splosna plovba supervisory board opts for privatisation and the search of strategic partner Friday/10 July - Krsko: Krsko Nuclear Power Plant Interim Board of Directors session ends unsuccessfully 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA Slovene Central Bank Has Stopped Intervening on Foreign Money Markets 

 The Bank of Slovenia announced the period of intervention by setting purchase prices of foreign currencies ended on Wednesday. The banks selected according to the bid are no longer obliged to keep up the intervention purchase price as of 9 July. 

 GOVERNMENT Hike in Electricity Price Rejected; Reports on Processing Industry and Slovene Ironworks Discussed 

 The government rejected at its session Thursday a proposal made by Eles, a power transmission enterprise, to rise the price of electricity by 14.5 percent as of 1 July. The latest rise took place on 1 January (8 percent). Reports prepared by the Economics Minister on the situation in the processing industry were confirmed by the government, together with measures to improve the condition of the procession industry which will be sent to parliament. The government also debated the report on the iron-manufacturing companies gathered in the Slovene Ironworks (SZ), establishing that reorganization in the branch was bearing fruit. 

 INTERNATIONAL ACTIVITIES Multilateral Screening for Fisheries 

 The Slovene delegation on Monday attended the multilateral screening, with the other five European Union membership applicants, for the common fisheries policy. Delegations of Slovenia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Estonia and Cyprus and European Commission enlargement group members examined the development of capacity to implement and enforce the common fisheries legislation. Bilateral screening for fisheries for Slovenia is scheduled for 14 July. 

 EU-Slovenia Subcommittee about Mid-Term Guidelines for Economic Development 

 The EU-Slovenia Subcommittee on Economic Issues was harmonizing Monday a draft Joint Assessment of Mid-Term Economic Policy Priorities of Slovenia. Divided in three chapters, the Joint Assessment analyzes the current economic situation in Slovenia, points to some economic problems and manners of settling them plus defines a medium-term macroeconomic target scenario. It in fact represents a common idea of what policy should be adopted to transform successfully the Slovene economy and prepare it for membership of the EU. 

 ECONOMIC-SOCIAL COUNCIL Grey Economy Prevention Bill Should be Passed Soon 

 The Economic and Social Council on Wednesday discussed and passed a bill aimed to prevent black economy. Social partners said the bill was good and had to be adopted as soon as possible. It will make a major contribution to improve the situation in the area, Minister of Labour and Council Chairman Anton Rop said. The session, which was attended also by European Affairs Minister Igor Bavcar, passed the decision to appoint representatives of the trade unions and employers, one of each, to the working groups reviewing the agreement of Slovenia's legislation with that of the EU. Grey economy has been increasing constantly over the last years also in Slovenia, where the share of moonlighting amounts to 17-22 percent of gross domestic product. 

 PRIVATISATION Gov't Passes Decree to Close Tally Accounts of Voucher Owners 

 The government on Wednesday issued a decree on the procedure to close tally accounts of privatisation voucher owners and enable the use of vouchers on the basis of the act on the conclusion of privatisation and privatisation of legal entities owned by the Slovene Development Company. The decree took immediate effect, It regulates the procedure of tally accounts closing; the procedure of exchange of vouchers for shares in internal distribution or internal buy-out in those companies in which these will be carried out by the end of October as well as the procedure of using vouchers in privatisation of the Triglav National Park Development Promotion Fund. 

 Privatisation Report in Slovene, English and German 

 The national Agency for Restructuring and Privatisation on Thursday presented a publication Privatisation Report, published in Slovene, English and German. According to the Report, the performance of privatised companies has improved during the last 3 years, but there is quite a difference between internally owned companies and companies controlled by outside owners. 

 VALUE ADDED TAX Finance Ministry on VAT 

 The Ministry of Finance on Friday organized the first working meeting with the press concerned with the introduction of value added tax. From now on such meetings will take place every week. The first one dealt with two topics: VAT exemption and VAT zero rate. 

 CONFERENCES Seminar within the 'Educate for Europe' Programme 

 The Slovene Management Research Institute on Tuesday organized a seminar on 'Liberalization, Privatization, Integration and Concentration on Finance and Capital Markets'. The seminar was addressed by France Arhar, the governor of Slovenia's central bank, who said the privatization of the greatest Slovene commercial banks Nova Ljubljanska banka and Nova kreditna banka Maribor was not to be carried out headlong. Such educational seminars are aimed to inform the participants, the leading managers of Slovene economy, about the economic, system and market conditions of Slovenia's adjusting to Europe. 

 ENERGY Krsko N-Plant Generated 425,000 MWh in June 

 The Krsko Nuclear Power Plant operated at full capacity and 95.4-percent capacity utilization last June, generating 425,847 megawatt-hours of electricity. 

 Krsko Interim Board of Directors Session Unsuccessful 

 The interim board of directors of the Krsko nuclear power plant failed to agree on any of the items on agenda of the session held on Friday at Krsko. Krsko CEO Ivo Banic, also director of the national power company Elektro-Slovenija (Eles), said problems appeared as early as at the session agenda. The session was discontinued after four hours when due to opposing views by Croatian members the board failed to reach agreement on the first two items on the agenda, concerning the selection of an international auditor to revise Krsko operations in the 1986-1996 period, and modernization funding. 

 TOURISM Higher Prices of Tourist Services Result in Less Tourist 

 Trends in the Slovene tourist industry ahead of the high season were presented at a news conference on Wednesday by the Ministry of Small Business and Tourism and the Slovene Tourist Board. Seemingly downward trends in the first third of 1998 resulted from the 'green' winter in the season of 1997/98, a rise in prices of tourist services, unemployment in some Western countries, the financial crisis in Asia and therefore low prices in the Far East, the fear that the Kosovo conflict might spread to Slovenia, the fact that the Slovene currency is overvalued, and perhaps also the EXPO world exhibition in Lisbon and the Football World Cup, Minister of Small Business and Tourism Janko Razgorsek said. In the January-to-April period, Slovene tourist destinations were visited by 1 percent less tourists than in the same period 1997, with overnight stays going down just the same. The number of foreign tourists in the same period fell 1 percent, too, but overnight stays made by them decreased by 2 percent. While there were less tourists from Austria, Belgium, Switzerland, the Netherlands and Germany, more guests came from Hungary, Italy, Great Britain, the USA, Croatia and Russia. 

 COMPANIES Kovinotehna Explains Changes in Management and Presents Plans 

 Representatives of Kovinotehna, a Celje-based trade company, on Tuesday talked about the reasons for changes in the management. Supervisory Board on Friday, 3 July, unanimously accepted the resignation of the management, who had established they were not achieving the 1998 targets on the basis of previous operation results analysis. The company's officials presented their plans for the future. Supervisory Board appointed Aleksander Ivan Gerzina new Management Board Chairman, observing the proposal of outgoing Chairman Ales Ilc. 

 Autocommerce Becomes Owner of Globtour Praha Travel Agency 

 Autocommerce, a Ljubljana-based joint-stock company, acquired a majority stake in Globtour Praha, one of the three largest tour operators in the Czech Republic, in the first half of July. Autocommerce thus continues with the implementation of its strategic objective to develop its tourist activities by investing in successful tourist companies engaged in organizing travels in a wider geographic area. 

 Port of Koper Holds 3rd General Assembly 

 Port of Koper shareholders allocated 1997 profit and undistributed profit from previous years at the third general assembly on Friday. They elected a new member of the nine-member supervisory board, and postponed deliberations on a proposal to reduce capital stock until autumn. It was decided that SIT 500 million (US$ 2.9m) of the SIT 1.9 (US$ 11.6m) net profit be allocated for the own share fund and SIT 1.4 billion (US$ 8.2m) remain undistributed. Of the undistributed profit from previous years amounting to SIT 837 million (US$ 4.9m), SIT 212 million (US$ 1.2m) belongs to the government according to the general assembly decision; SIT 8.5 million was allocated for awards to supervisory board members, and SIT 614 million (US$ 3.6m) for dividends. Gross dividend will thus amount to SIT 86 (US$ .508) per share. 

 Petrol Presents Modernized Laboratory 

 Slovene oil company Petrol's management team on Thursday presented a modernized chemical laboratory, the only Slovene chemical laboratory with the accreditation of the Office for Standardization and Metrology. The laboratory has gained the title of the central Slovene oil laboratory. Representatives of Petrol spoke also about the current business operations, a annual general meeting to be held on 31 July and problems regarding Slovenia's oil refinery Nafta Lendava, owned by Petrol, the majority stakeholder, and the government (45 percent). 

 Slovene Shipowner's Board Opt for Privatisation 

 Supervisory Board of Splosna plovba on Friday examined an analysis of conceivable ways of privatisation of the only Slovene shipowner. Board members established the analysis indicated good starting points for a successful realization of company's privatisation as it considered the agreement for a 20-percent workers' share and demands by the Banka Koper bank. Wishing to secure state property, Supervisory Board advocated the idea that a strategic partner be found by international tender. 

 Kolicevo Paper Mill Changes Hands 

 The ownership structure in the Sarrio Slovenija paper mill has changed: the 40-percent stake of Italy's Sarrio SA was bought by Austria's Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG. The company's new name is Kolicevo Karton d.o.o.. 

 Acroni Exceeds Sales Targets 

 Acroni of Jesenice sold 94,000 tons of goods in the first six months, exceeding the target amount by 15 percent. The loss amounted to SIT 600 million in the period, while the annual plan had been set at one billion tolars. Acroni is a metallurgical company operating within the Slovene Ironworks concern. 

 STATISTICS Slovenia's Foreign Exchange Reserves Total US$ 4.31 Billion 

 Slovenia's foreign exchange reserves amounted to US$ 4.31 billion in end-April, a rise of US$ 77.5 million, or 1.8 percent over March. Foreign exchange reserves of the central bank allowed for US$ 3.3 billion (77 percent) and those of commercial banks US$ 981 million. Foreign currency reserves increased by US$ 55 million in end-April over the beginning of 1998, when they reached US$ 4.26 billion. 

 Foreign Trade Declined in May 

 Slovenia's exports totaled US$ 736.6 million in May and were down by 1.9 percent from a month before, with imports down by 5.6 percent to US$ 809.9 million. The deficit amounted to US$ 73.3 million at a 90.9-percent exports/imports ratio. Compared to May 1997, exports rose by 8.5 percent and imports by 2.4 percent. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE Shares Up on Ljubljana Stock Exchange 

 All three markets within the Ljubljana Stock Exchange recorded appreciations in shares last week. The SBI share index was slightly down only on Monday, and then up in the following days. It increased by 52.94 points and concluded the week at 1743.51 points. The opposite trend was recorded in the BIO bond index; it was down by 0.34 points to 104.02 points. 

 EXCHANGE RATES Most Leading Foreign Currencies Appreciate 

 The mean prices of leading foreign currencies increased last week according to the Bank of Slovenia. The U.S. dollar was up by SIT 0.84 to SIT 171.09, the German mark by SIT 0.05 to SIT 93.85 and the Austrian schilling by SIT 0.01 to SIT 13.34. A decline was recorded in the Swiss franc, by SIT 0.31 to SIT 111.11, while the mean price of the Italian lira remained unchanged at SIT 9.52 for 100 liras.

title: Bank of  Slovenia  ends tolar rate  intervention .
text:
LJUBLJANA, July 8 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Wednesday it would on Thursday end the tolar exchange rate intervention it began at the end of May. 

 "From July 9 the cooperating banks are no longer obliged to maintain the intervention tolar exchange rate," the bank said in a statement. 

 At the end of May, the central bank said banks cooperating with its exchange rate intervention would have to buy foreign currency from companies at a minimum rate of 93.9 tolars to the German mark. 

 The minimum rate was raised to 94.1 on June 15 and to 94.4 on July 2. 

 Following the intervention, the banks' exchange rate for companies rose to an average of about 94.5 tolars to the mark from 93.5 tolars at the end of May and 94.4 tolars at the start of the year. 

 The central bank said it would continue to buy foreign exchange from those commercial banks that bought at least 90 percent of all foreign exchange from companies at a rate no lower than the last tolar intervention exchange rate. 

 Banks wanting to sell foreign exchange to the central bank will also have to have a mark exchange rate for citizens no lower than 0.2 percent below the last intervention rate of 94.4 tolars. 

 ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Slovene  Central Bank  Has Stopped  Intervening  on Foreign Money Markets.
text:
Ljubljana, 8 July (STA) - The Bank of Slovenia has said the period of intervention by setting purchase prices of foreign currencies ended on Wednesday. The decision was adopted on Wednesday by the central bank governor, following the bid for intervention in foreign money markets by means of intervention purchase price dating from 27 May. The banks selected according to the bid are no longer obliged to keep up the intervention purchase price as of 9 July, the Bank of Slovenia reported. 

 The central bank on 2 July sent the bid for temporary intervention purchase of foreign exchange with the obligatory return purchase in two months to those banks which have signed an agreement on cooperation in foreign money markets intervention with the Bank of Slovenia. The banks were entitled to lower exchange rates for the purchase of foreign cash in exchange offices for a maximum of 0.2 percent for D-Mark, and 0.4 percent for other currencies.

title: Bank of  Slovenia  raises tolar  intervention  rate.
text:
LJUBLJANA, July 2 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Thursday banks cooperating in its exchange rate intervention will from Thursday have to buy foreign currency from companies at a minimum of 94.4 tolars to the mark, up from 93.9 tolars. 

 It said the central bank would in exchange buy marks from the cooperating banks at a rate of 94.6 tolars to the mark, up from a rate of 94.1 set at the end of May. 

 "Raising the intervention rate is in line with the bank's strategy regarding the appreciation of the tolar," Francek Drenovec, head of the central bank's analytic and research centre, told Reuters. 


The Bank of Slovenia started intervening at the end of May to slow the appreciation of the tolar, cooperating with Nova Ljubljanska Banka, SKB  , Dolenjska Banka		   , Banka Celje and Abanka.



On Thursday, the tolar stood at 93.76 to the mark compared with 94.4 tolars at the start of 1998. ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545, ljubljana.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: FOCUS-Bank of Slovenia slows tolar strengthening.
text:
LJUBLJANA, July 2 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia on Thursday intervened on the local foreign exchange market for the third time in six weeks to rein in the appreciation of the tolar currency. 

 Economists said the central bank's policy was proving a success and should have been implemented earlier. 

 "In fact it should have come some five months earlier," Franci Krizanic, an economist at Ljubljana University's Faculty of Law, told Reuters. 

 "Had the bank not intervened, the appreciation of the tolar would seriously hurt Slovenian exporters and their profitability which could cause reduction of exports and....a lack of foreign currency," he added. 

 Slovenia has seen its currency appreciate over the last few years due to high foreign exchange inflows from exports, foreign investment and tourism. 

 "The central bank's goal is to neutralise surplus foreign inflows in order to reach a stable tolar exchange rate," Bank of Slovenia Governor France Arhar told Reuters earlier. 

 Maintaining a stable tolar exchange rate and controlling inflation were the bank's main goals. 

 In its latest move on Thursday, the central bank said banks cooperating in its exchange rate intervention would have to buy foreign currency from companies at a minimum of 94.4 tolars to the mark, compared to 94.1 tolars since June 15 and 93.9 tolars since the end of May. 

 "Raising the intervention rate is in line with the bank's strategy regarding the appreciation of the tolar," Francek Drenovec, head of the central bank's analytic and research centre, told Reuters. 


The Bank of Slovenia started intervening at the end of May, cooperating with Nova Ljubljanska Banka, SKB  , Dolenjska Banka		   , Banka Celje and Abanka.



Bankers expect the Bank of Slovenia to raise the intervention exchange rate at least once a month over the next five months.



"If the central bank wants to reduce the difference between the exchange rate and inflation it will have to raise the tolar rate to the mark by about 0.6 tolars each month," said Vanda Mocnik Kohek, head of treasury at Bank Austria.



Slovenia's consumer price index rose 4.9 percent from the end of December to the end of June but the government is still forecasting that price inflation for the whole year will be eight percent, down from 8.4 percent in 1997. Analysts said the government may slow the pace of increases in officially-controlled fuel and electricty prices in order to hit that target.

title: Weekly Review of Slovene Economy from June 14 through 20.
text:
Ljubljana, 20 June (STA) - President of the Chamber of Small Business (OZS) Transport Section Darko Hlupic officially called off a protest of truck drivers scheduled for Monday, 22 June, after an agreement was signed on Friday afternoon between the government, Chamber of Small Business (OZS) and Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GZS). At Friday's correspondence session, the government adopted several measures thus meeting the demands made by Slovene truck drivers. The government agreed to reduce motorway tolls and yearly payments for the use of roads which in the future would be calculated on the basis of lorry axle pressure and the lorry's weight, as stipulated by the EU standards. Moreover, it was agreed that in the border area at border crossings and on national roads the government will not allow the collection of municipality taxes. 

  By 2 July at the latest, the government will have adopted a decree (which will take effect on 15 July) allowing lorries to have a free access to the customs house. By 30 October, a working group should bring some other issues into line with truck drivers' demands, one of which is a change to the recently passed Road Safety Act. Minister of Transport and Communications Anton Bergauer said a working group would start dealing with the remaining open issues as early as on Monday. 

 Chronology: Wednesday/17 June - Ljubljana: Trade union SKEI congres; Wednesday/17 June - Ljubljana: Three-day meeting of high-ranking representatives of the nuclear safety administrations in the EU, Central and Eastern Europe and former Soviet Union nations, taking place in the framework of Concert Group; Wednesday/17 June - Celje: The beginning of the fair 'For A Healthier Life with Nature'; Thursday/18 June - Ljubljana: The beginning of 27th regular annual economic colloquium of NATO; Thursday/18 June - Ljubljana: Resumption of negotiations to conclude a new social agreement. 

 GOVERNMENT Slovenia temporarily abolished concessions for the import of wheat from Hungary 

 For the first time since Slovenia has become a member of CEFTA, the Slovene government on 18th June adopted a protective customs measure, the aim of which is to reduce the import of inexpensive wheat from Hungary. With the modification of the decree on temporary use of additional protocol no. 6 to CEFTA agreement, it temporarily abolished the 15-percent preferential customs rate for the import of wheat and replaced it by a regular 5.3-percent customs rate and a special import levy (SIT 17.2). The customs duty for the import of wheat from Hungary has thus increased by 7.5 percent. 

 Employment Programme Adopted 

 The government passed on 18 June an active employment policy programme for 1998 in an effort to reduce unemployment by 5000 to 10,000 persons. According to Minister of Labour Anton Rop, the programme is designed both for those unemployed and those workers whose job is uncertain. A part of the employment policy programme is also the scheme to reorganize enterprises, carried out by the Slovene Development Corporation (SRD). Two basic schemes on which the active employment policy programme is based are a programme to train the unemployed and a public works programme. The two programmes are expected to involve 10,000 unemployed. SIT 16 billion is to be allocated for their implementation. 

 EU - SLOVENIA Legislation of EU Candidates in Area of Free Movement of Goods Screened 

 Slovene producers should not face any severe difficulties when EU standards are enforced, said State Secretary in the Slovene Ministry of Economic Relations and Development Vojka Ravbar, who attended a week-long multilateral meeting at which EU candidates' legislation regulating the free movement of goods was screened. Nevertheless, Slovenia will have to adopt several regulations to do away with some technical obstacles obstructing the free movement of goods, and apply them, too. Slovenia is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with EU officials at which the same topic will be discussed on 30 June, to wind up on 8 July. 

 Slovene Agriculture Presented to European Negotiators 

 Slovene Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Forestry officials briefed a EU delegation on visit to Slovenia on 18 June about Slovenia's integration into the EU from the aspect of agriculture. The visiting EU delegation consisted of head of the EU negotiating team with EU candidates Nikolaus van der Pas, chief negotiator in charge of Slovenia Jaime Garcia Lombardero and head of the European Commission delegation to Slovenia Amir Naqvi. EU officials were updated on the situation in Slovene agriculture, and compared it with agriculture in some other EU candidates; they were also informed about how Slovenia is preparing its agriculture for EU membership. 

 BUSINESS CONFERENCES, CONSULTATIONS Slovene Enterprises Want to Increase Exports to Poland 

 Polish experts presented the characteristics of the Polish market and specific ways of marketing industrial products and consumer goods there at a seminar entitled How to Export to Poland, organized for Slovene business people by the Trade and Investment Promotion Office and business magazine Gospodarski Vestnik. The seminar was attended by over 40 representatives of Slovene business that are interested in exporting to the 40-million Polish market. The Slovene-Polish trade is marked by a surplus of some US$ 100 million on the Slovene side. With Poland buying a lot of Slovene products, its main imports from Slovenia are pharmaceutical products, whose worth reached US$ 60 million last year, and electric switches. 

 A Conference of Slovene and Belgian Business Officials 

 A Slovene-Belgian business conference was organized in the framework of the visit by a Belgian business delegation to Slovenia on 16 June by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia (CCIS). It was attended by 14 Belgian companies from the field of agriculture and food industry, metal and chemical industries and banking as well as 32 Slovene companies. A cooperation agreement between the CCIS of the Belgian Foreign Trade Board was signed on the occasion by Matevz Bambic, head of the CCIS department for international cooperation, and Paul Vindelinckx, secretary general of the Belgian Board. Trade between Slovenia and Belgium amounted to US$ 101.1 million in the first four months of this year, which is nearly by 20 percent more than in the same period last year. 

 COMPANIES The Most Successful Slovene Companies in 1997 

 Company Revoz from Novo mesto heads the list of 300 biggest Slovene companies with regard to revenue in 1997. Petrol and Elektro Slovenija are placed second and third in the list, respectively, followed by Poslovni sistem Mercator and Gorenje from Velenje. The total revenue of Revoz amounted to SIT 156 billion, the revenue of Petrol amounted to SIT 128 billion, and the revenue of Elektro Slovenija to SIT 87 billion. With net profit amounting to SIT 5.7 billion, Telekom Slovenije - according to unaudited data - is placed first on the list of the most successful Slovene companies regarding the net profit. The pharmaceutical company Krka is placed second with net profit amounting to SIT 5.1 billion in 1997, and the pharmaceutical company Lek is placed third with the net profit of SIT 3.7 billion in 1997. 

 Iskrateling Signed a Deal with Russians 

 Slovenia's Iskrateling has recently signed a contract with Russia's North Caucasus Railways. The equipment supplied and installed by Iskrateling will launch the digitalization of the railway network there. Iskrateling will supply 237 digital telephone exchanges and install optical cables. Apart from telephone exchanges, Iskrateling will provide the other teleinformation equipment necessary for the operator. The first deal is worth US$ 12 million. The railway of the region of North Caucasus is among the largest of a total of 17 railway regions in Russia. With its routs totaling some 7000 km, North Caucasus Railways employ 120,000 workers. Iskrateling is negotiating similar contracts with some other Russian railways. 

 Bankruptcy Proceedings of Delta Ptuj 

 Bankruptcy proceedings were initiated for the company Delta in Ptuj, which employs 330 people. The decision was reached on 15 June by the management of Labod and trade unions representatives. 180 of the employed will be temporarily included in the other Labod's company in Ptuj, the company Valida, whereas the other employees will be directed to the National Employment Office. 

 British Airways Opened Its Branch Office in Ljubljana 

 The company British Airways opened its branch office on 16 June in Ljubljana. Apart from selling tickets, the company will also be offering services of its subsidiary company British Airways Holidays. 

 233,800 Passengers Travelled with Adria Airways in the First Five Months 

 As many as 233,800 passengers travelled by Adria Airways' aeroplanes in the first five months of this year, which is by 14 percent more than in the same period last year. The number of passengers increased by 18 percent in the regular passenger services and by four percent in charter. Adria also transported 1490 tons of cargo in the first five months, which is by three percent less than in the same period last year. 

 COMPANIES - GENERAL MEETINGS Cinkarna is to Pay Out Dividends, Last Year's Loss Covered 

 Cinkarna Celje shareholders discussed at the first general meeting on 16 June the shareout of profits since 1993 and last year's loss. The company registered SIT 574 million of revalued profit in the period from 1993 to 1995. They will allocate 39.74 percent of the profit to pay out the dividends, whereas 60 percent of the profit will not be allocated. The total loss of Cinkarna Celje amounted to SIT 230 million last year. 

 Ljubljana Stock Exchange Shareholders Hold General Meeting 

 Ljubljana Stock Exchange shareholders approved the 1997 business report and decided not to divide last year's clear profit of SIT 332.8 thousand. A change passed by the general meeting was that the number of members of the supervisory board would be reduced from 11 to 7. The market capitalization of shares listed on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange increased a great deal in 1997. Another significant factor influencing last year's business operations was the introduction of the fiduciary accounts by the Bank of Slovenia. 

 Lek Share Brings a Dividend of SIT 660 

 Lek shareholders adopted some changes to the joint-stock company's statute, passed the 1997 business report, discussed the division of their profit and elected new members of the supervisory board. Lek's clear profit amounted to SIT 3.7 billion in 1997, a rise of 21 percent over 1996, Management Board Director Andro Ocvirk told news conference on Friday. Net profit per share totaled SIT 1,914 last year. While last year's clear profit remains undivided, Lek will divide clear profit made in previous years (amounting to SIT 1.3 billion). The divided per share (either A, B or C) will total SIT 660. The general meeting, held on Thursday, reached two decisions to change the Lek statute. The changes will apply to dematerialization of shares A and B. Director Ocvirk said the company's business operations were positively influenced also by the 12.9-percent growth rate of U.S. dollar exchange rate in 1997. Lek managed to register its drug aciclovir in the U.S. market, one of its key foreign markets. Together with amocsiclav and cimetidin, aciclovir is Lek's major product. Mostly owing to an increase in exports, Lek's revenues totaled SIT 21 billion in the January-to-May period, 15 percent up from the same period 1997. Foreigners hold a 30-percent share of Lek, with Slovene investment funds holding nearly the same share. 

 BANK OF SLOVENIA New Intervention Purchase Exchange Rate 

 The Bank of Slovenia informed on 15 June about the new intervention purchase exchange rate, amounting to SIT 94.10 per German mark. The banks, which were chosen on the basis of the proposal and are obliged to buy the foreign currency on the basis of the intervention purchase exchange rate, started to use the new intervention purchase exchange rate on 16 June. 

 Governors of Central Banks of All Former Yugoslav Republics Meet 

 A meeting of governors of central banks of all former Yugoslav republics, first after seven years, was held in Brussels at the initiative of Alfons Verplaetse, Belgian governor and Chairman of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Bank of Slovenia reported on Tuesday. The talks, held on Monday, centred on economic situation in the new-formed countries and on the results of monetary policies in the new situation. The governors also discussed possibilities for distribution of the property of the former central bank of Yugoslavia (NBJ) at the Basel Bank, in particular certain options presented by Governor Verplaetse. The governors agreed a new meeting should be organized as soon as possible, the Bank of Slovenia reported. 

 Watts: New Round of Negotiations on Succession to Ex-Yugoslavia in Autumn 

 Sir Arthur Watts, international mediator for negotiations on succession to former Yugoslavia, will start a new round of negotiations with the successor states in September. At their meeting on Wednesday, Watts also informed Slovenia's Foreign Minister Boris Frlec that he would visit Slovenia in September or October. According to Watts, the forthcoming round of negotiations will be the last chance before the international community decides for arbitration. Minister Frlec, who is paying a two-day visit to London, explained to Watts that it was in the interest of Ljubljana for the succession issue to be solved as soon as possible. In his opinion, the solution would also contribute to the normalization of relations between the successor states and to economic and political stability in the region. Slovenia believes that solution of the succession problem would not only help stabilize South-Eastern Europe but would also have a positive impact on the solution of the Kosovo crisis. 

 BANKS Hmezad banka to Merge with Banka Celje this September 

 The General Meeting of the Hmezad banka Zalec bank on 15 June passed a resolution to merge with Banka Celje. As proposed by the managements of both banks, the merger will be carried out on 30 September 1998. Hmezad banka decided to merge with the Celje bank to economize operating, globalize banking transactions, expand the range of services and last but not least to cushion restricted conditions of bank operations and severer foreign competitions. After the merger Hmezad banka will operate as Banka Celje, Zalec subsidiary. Hmezad banka was set up in 1992. A universal bank, Hmezad is licenced to conduct all banking operations except the foreign currency deposits of individuals. The banks Banka Celje and Hmezad banka signed a contract to set up the banking group Banka Celje in January 1997. 

 Bank of Celje's 1997 Net Profit Over 1 Billion Tolars 

 The 1997 net profit of Bank of Celje amounted to SIT 1.2 billion tolars (USD 72 million). The 1997 income totalled SIT 17 billion while the expenses amounted to SIT 15.7 billion. Bank of Celje increased its market share from 5.14 percent to 5.21 percent and confirmed its position as the fifth biggest bank in Slovenia (of the total of 28). 

 TRANSPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS State Guarantees for Loans Taken up to Build a Railway Line between Puconci and Hungarian Border 

 The National Assembly adopted through a fast-track procedure a law on state guarantees for loans taken up by Slovene Railways to build a railway line between Puconci and the Hungarian border. The principals of the loans taken up must not exceed ECU 71.3 million (SIT 13.2 billion). 

 POWER SUPPLY The Government Appointed a Negotiating Group for Power Plant Krsko 

 The government agreed to the initiative on 11 June to conclude an interstate agreement between Slovenia and Croatia connected with the proprietorship and the status of the power plant. The government appointed the negotiating group, consisting of 14-members and led by Uros Korze. The initiative to conclude the agreement was sent to the parliament and is to be discussed by the international relations committee. 

 Geoplin Lowered the Natural Gas by 10 Percent 

 The company Geoplin lowered on 16 June the price of natural gas by ten percent. The reduction will be in force by the end of this September. The price of natural gas will amount to SIT 20.6 per cubic meter in average. 

 UNEMPLOYMENT Unemployment Decreasing for the Fourth Month in SuccessionThe National Employment Office provided employment to 56,000 unemployed people last year, and included 32,000 unemployed people and 8,000 redundant workers in employment programmes. It offered assistance to 50,000 employers, enabled unemployment benefits to nearly 41,000 unemployed people and provided scholarships to 55,000 college and university students. 124,552 people were registered at the National Employment Office at the end of May, which is by 1.7 percent more than in May 1997. The unemployment is decreasing for the fourth month in succession currently. The level of unemployment was 14.4 percent in May; 13.5 percent among men and 15.6 percent among women. 

 STATISTICS GDP Increased by 1.9 Percent in the First Quarter 

 Gross domestic product (GDP) in fixed prices dating from 1992 increased by 1.9 percent in the first quarter of 1998 compared with the last quarter of the previous year; this is by 0.6 percent higher growth than in the previous quarter (1.3 percent). The growth rate on the annual level also shows strong rise; GDP was in the first quarter of this year by 6.5 percent higher over the first quarter in 1997. Slovenia has not registered such a high growth rate (on the annual level) since the second quarter of 1994. 

 April Net Salary SIT 97,993 

 The average net salary in Slovene companies and other organizations amounted to SIT 97,993 in April, the National Statistical office reported. The average April net salary was by 0.6 percent higher than in March and by 9.8 percent higher than in April 1997. The average gross salary in Slovenia amounted to SIT 155,145 in April, which is by 0.9 percent more than a year ago. 

 STOCK EXCHANGE The Majority of Shares Decreased in Price 

 The SBI share index fell under 1700 points last week one more time, having lost 37.88 points to 1663.51 points. Seventeen shares depreciated on stock market listings and ten appreciated at Ljubljana Stock Exchange. The BIO bond index was up by 0.15 point to 103.96 points. 

 EXCHANGE RATES U.S. Dollar and Swiss Franc Down 

 Last week saw a decrease in price of the U.S. dollar (by SIT 1.3 to SIT 167.90) and the Swiss franc (by SIT 1.2 to SIT 111.96). The price for 100 Italian lira remained almost unchanged at SIT 9.50 per 100 liras, whereas the Austrain schilling and the German mark increased slightly - by SIT 0.1 to SIT 13.31 and by SIT 0.06 to SIT 93.66, respectively.

title: Bank of  Slovenia intervenes  to slow tolar rise.
text:
LJUBLJANA, May 29 (Reuters) - The Bank of Slovenia said on Friday from this week it would buy foreign currency from five commercial banks at a minimum rate of 94.1 tolars to the mark to slow the appreciation of the tolar. 

 The rate for other currencies will be fixed according to their Frankfurt rate against mark, the bank said. 

 "We want to reduce the difference between tolar exchange rates and inflation. Since September the tolar has appreciated six to eight percent against the main currencies in which we conduct our foreign trade," Francek Drenovec, head of the central bank's analytic and research centre, told Reuters. 

 While the tolar had eased slightly on the foreign exchanges since September, in real terms it had appreciated substantially because of high domestic inflation, Drenovec said. 

 Slovenia's main foreign trade currencies are the German mark, Italian lira, Austrian shilling, French franc, Swiss franc, U.S. dollar and British pound. 

 On Friday the tolar stood at 93.47 to the mark, compared to 94.4 tolars at the start of 1998 and 92.63 tolars at the start of September 1997. 

 Slovenia's consumer price index rose by 8.8 percent in 1997, but in the first five months of 1998 it has risen a further 4.9 percent. 

 The central bank said it would buy foreign currency from Nova Ljubljanska Banka, SKB  , Dolenjska Banka, Banka Celje and Abanka, who are in turn obliged to buy foreign currency from companies at a minimum price of 93.9 tolars to the mark. 

 The five banks account for over 40 percent of Slovenia's currency trade between banks and companies. ((Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-17-00-545)).

title: Bank of Slovenia to Participate in Foreign Money Markets.
text:
Ljubljana, 27 May (STA) - Bank of Slovenia's Council passed the following decisions at its 161st session on Monday: 

 The Bank of Slovenia will actively engage in foreign money markets. The banks that the Bank of Slovenia will sign cooperation agreements with after selecting them in public tenders will be allowed to purchase foreign currencies at SIT 93.90 per Deutsche mark from 25 May onwards. 

 The selected banks will be entitled to lower exchange rates for the purchase of foreign cash in exchange offices for a maximum of 0.2 percent for Deutsche marks, and 0.4 percent for other currencies. 

 The Bank of Slovenia will have the right to change intervention conditions in accordance with foreign money market trends and monetary policy objectives. The central bank will inform the public about the selected banks, through which interventions in foreign money markets will be conducted, on Thursday, 28 May. 

 The Council also amended the decision on the Bank of Slovenia unbalanced foreign currency assets and liabilities (the bank's open foreign currency position), stipulating that the banks will have to balance their open foreign currency positions on a monthly basis. The decision will take effect upon publication in the Official Gazette. 

 The Council confirmed the June foreign exchange minimum of SIT 362,934 million, down 0.3 percent from the previous month. 

 The Council also adopted the report on the use of contemporary payment instruments in the first quarter of 1998, pointing out bank risks the are increasingly present in the constantly rising volume of credit card operations.
